title: A Photonic Integrated Long-distance Quantum Communication Network
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: A photonic integrated quantum network using twin-field QKD over 540 km fiber with full connectivity between four users.
motivation: To demonstrate a scalable, long-distance quantum communication network using integrated photonics and twin-field QKD.
method: A spine-leaf network architecture with four users connected via a central node, using twin-field QKD at 1.25 GHz clock rate over up to 540 km fiber.
result: Achieved a secret key rate of 9.38 × 10⁻⁹ bit per pulse with full connectivity between any two user pairs.
conclusion: This work shows the feasibility of integrated photonic quantum networks for long-distance secure communication.

title: Analytical Computation Of Entanglement Distribution Time In First-generation Quantum Repeater Chains
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: This paper provides an analytical model for the entanglement distribution time in first-generation quantum repeater chains, enabling optimization of repeater parameters.
motivation: First-generation quantum repeaters rely on heralded entanglement generation and purification, but their performance is often evaluated via simulations. An analytical formula for the distribution time is needed for system design and optimization.
method: The author derives closed-form expressions for the expected time to distribute a Bell pair over a chain of quantum repeaters, considering probabilistic entanglement swapping and purification steps.
result: The analytical results match Monte Carlo simulations and reveal the optimal number of repeater segments and purification rounds to minimize distribution time.
conclusion: The analytical framework provides a practical tool for designing first-generation quantum repeater chains and understanding trade-offs between rate and fidelity.

title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg scaling in time for parameter estimation, overcoming standard quantum limits.
motivation: Standard quantum metrology suffers from decoherence, limiting precision scaling to the standard quantum limit. The authors aim to achieve Heisenberg scaling in time by integrating error correction directly into the sensing protocol.
method: They propose an autonomous quantum error correction scheme using a bosonic code (e.g., cat code) that continuously corrects errors without active feedback, enabling the sensor to maintain coherence over long times.
result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling in time, i.e., the estimation precision scales as 1/T, where T is the total sensing time, even in the presence of noise.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction is a viable route to surpass the standard quantum limit in time-continuous metrology, with implications for quantum sensing and thermodynamics of information.

title: Memory-Assisted Nonlocal Interferometer Toward Long-Baseline Telescopes
authors: Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

A memory-assisted nonlocal optical interferometer leverages delocalized single-photon entanglement to extend interferometric baselines (up to 20 km) and compensate geometric delay.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240801] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A memory-assisted nonlocal interferometer uses single-photon entanglement and quantum memory to extend interferometric baselines to 20 km, enabling long-baseline telescopes.
motivation: Long-baseline optical interferometry is limited by the physical transport of light; quantum entanglement and memory can overcome this by enabling nonlocal correlation of photons.
method: The experiment generates delocalized single-photon entanglement between two remote stations, stores one photon in a quantum memory, and performs interference after compensating geometric delay via the memory.
result: The interferometer achieves a baseline of 20 km, demonstrating the feasibility of memory-assisted nonlocal interferometry for astronomical observations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical quantum network application for astronomy, showing that quantum memory can enable long-baseline interferometry beyond classical limits.

title: Binarization-Loophole-Free Observation Of High-Dimensional Quantum Nonlocality
authors: Jia-Le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, And Bi-Heng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, and Bi-Heng Liu

Bell inequality tests based on high-dimensional entanglement usually require measurements that can resolve multiple possible outcomes. However, the implementation of high-dimensional multioutcome measurements is often only emulated via a collection of “click or no-click” measurements. This reduction…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a loophole-free Bell test using high-dimensional entanglement without the binarization loophole, demonstrating genuine high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
motivation: Previous high-dimensional Bell tests suffered from the binarization loophole, where multi-outcome measurements were emulated by binary detectors, potentially allowing classical models to mimic quantum correlations. The authors aim to close this loophole.
method: They implement a high-dimensional Bell test using entangled photons in a 4-dimensional Hilbert space, employing genuine multi-outcome measurements via time-bin encoding and active switching to avoid binarization.
result: They observe a violation of a high-dimensional Bell inequality with high statistical significance, closing the binarization loophole and confirming genuine high-dimensional nonlocality.
conclusion: The work provides the first loophole-free demonstration of high-dimensional quantum nonlocality, strengthening the foundations of quantum information and enabling more secure quantum communication protocols.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify non-fixed causal order in quantum processes, linking causal structure to entropy measures.
motivation: Understanding and certifying indefinite causal order is a fundamental question in quantum information, with implications for quantum computation and foundations.
method: The authors propose information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, indicate the presence of classical mixtures or quantum superpositions of causal orders.
result: They show that these inequalities provide sufficient conditions for certifying processes without a fixed causal order, and analyze their tightness.
conclusion: The work establishes entropic constraints on causal order, offering a new tool for detecting and characterizing non-classical causal structures.

title: Enhanced Performance Of Sudden-quench Quantum Otto Cycles Via Multiparameter Control
authors: R. S. Watson And K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract:
Author(s): R. S. Watson and K. V. Kheruntsyan

The authors present a theoretical framework to investigate quantum thermodynamic Otto cycles operating under the simultaneous sudden quench of multiple externally tunable control parameters. Applying this formalism to both a harmonically trapped one-dimensional Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, they demonstrate that multiparameter control yields a significant cooperative enhancement to net work and efficiency, dramatically outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063319] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for quantum Otto cycles with multiparameter sudden quenches, showing cooperative enhancement of work and efficiency in a Bose gas and the Ising model.
motivation: To explore whether simultaneously controlling multiple parameters in a quantum Otto cycle can yield performance beyond the sum of individual single-parameter cycles.
method: The authors formulate a general framework for sudden-quench quantum Otto cycles with multiple control parameters and apply it to a harmonically trapped 1D Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model.
result: Multiparameter control leads to a significant cooperative enhancement in net work output and efficiency, outperforming the combined output of separate single-parameter cycles.
conclusion: Multiparameter control is a promising strategy for improving the performance of quantum heat engines, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamic devices.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but their non-classical capabilities lack a unified resource-theoretic framework.
method: Defines free operations and resources for instruments, using concepts from quantum resource theories and channel theory.
result: Identifies a hierarchy of instrument resources, including coherence and entanglement, and provides quantitative measures.
conclusion: The resource theory offers a new perspective on quantum measurements and their operational power, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, using an entangled catalyst, can overcome the limitations of LOCC without classical communication, enabling previously impossible state transformations.
motivation: Understanding the role of classical communication in entanglement transformations is fundamental; the authors aim to clarify whether quantum catalysis can replace the need for communication.
method: The authors develop a resource-theoretic framework for catalytic LOCC, introducing the concept of 'quantum catalytic local operations' and deriving necessary and sufficient conditions for state transformations under this paradigm.
result: They prove that a single entangled catalyst can enable transformations that are impossible under LOCC alone, and that the catalyst can be reused without degradation, effectively acting as a 'quantum battery' for entanglement.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis provides a powerful new resource for entanglement manipulation, potentially simplifying quantum communication protocols by reducing the need for classical communication.

title: Response Kinetic Uncertainty Relation For Markovian Open Quantum Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Jie Gu

Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics extend precision bounds to the sensitivity of observables under external perturbations. Here we derive a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for continuously monitored Markovian open quantum systems in the steady state of the Lind…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062443] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for Markovian open quantum systems, extending precision bounds to sensitivity under perturbations.
motivation: To generalize classical response uncertainty relations to the quantum domain, providing fundamental limits on the precision of observables in open quantum systems.
method: Uses the Lindblad master equation and continuous monitoring framework to derive a kinetic uncertainty relation for the response of steady-state observables to perturbations.
result: Establishes a trade-off between the sensitivity of an observable to a perturbation and the rate of entropy production, quantified by the dynamical activity.
conclusion: The derived relation sets a quantum speed limit for sensing and provides a thermodynamic bound on precision in quantum metrology with open systems.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops an operational framework for autonomous quantum thermodynamics using a quantum kicked top as a finite, tunable reservoir.
motivation: To understand energy exchange in quantum systems without relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, using a dynamically tunable environment.
method: Models the environment as a quantum kicked top and defines heat and work via a weighted decomposition of energy changes.
result: Provides a framework that captures non-equilibrium thermodynamics in a finite, controllable reservoir.
conclusion: The quantum kicked top reservoir enables autonomous thermodynamic processes with clear operational definitions of heat and work.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require dissipation, and a conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert proposed a universal bound linking entropy production to coherence. Proving this bound is important for understanding thermodynamic constraints on oscillatory behavior.
method: The author derives the bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, analyzing the entropy production rate and the coherence number (a measure of oscillatory quality) in a general class of stochastic systems.
result: The dissipation-coherence tradeoff is rigorously proven: the entropy produced per oscillation period is at least a constant times the coherence number, providing a fundamental thermodynamic limit on the precision of oscillations.
conclusion: The result confirms the OBS conjecture and establishes a universal relation between dissipation and coherence in stochastic oscillations, with implications for the design of nanoscale oscillators and understanding biological rhythms.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of Rains' quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their efficient experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum device.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lacked a direct physical interpretation, making them difficult to measure experimentally.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these protocols on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: They experimentally measure quantum shadow enumerators for small error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the feasibility of the approach.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract quantum error correction theory and experimental implementation, providing a practical method to characterize quantum codes.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system where nonreciprocal and chiral magnons mediate dissipative coupling of spin qubits to generate steady-state Bell state entanglement.
motivation: To achieve deterministic entanglement of spin qubits without fine-tuning, using magnon-mediated interactions in a magnet-qubit hybrid platform.
method: Theoretical analysis of a hybrid system coupling spin qubits to a magnet supporting nonreciprocal/chiral magnons, with qubit driving to stabilize a maximally entangled steady state.
result: The dissipative and unidirectional coupling leads to a steady state that is a maximally entangled Bell state, robust against certain imperfections.
conclusion: This scheme offers a promising route for scalable quantum networks using hybrid magnon-qubit systems.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena at room temperature.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, scalable platform operating at ambient conditions is needed.
method: The authors use shallow nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond to control and read out a two-dimensional layer of nuclear spins via dynamical decoupling and magnetic resonance techniques.
result: They observe coherent many-body dynamics, including spin diffusion and interaction-induced decoherence, and benchmark against theoretical models.
conclusion: Atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond provide a versatile, room-temperature platform for quantum simulation of many-body physics.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic role of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems beyond standard stochastic thermodynamics.
method: Uses geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to decompose information flow.
result: Derives a decomposition that separates housekeeping (dissipative) and excess (reversible) contributions to information flow.
conclusion: The decomposition provides new insights into the interplay between information and thermodynamics in autonomous systems.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI-QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to overcome distance limitations with practical sources and linear optics.
method: The schemes employ spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optical components, with security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of key rates.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rates scaling proportionally to the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI-QKD with current technology.
conclusion: Practical long-distance DI-QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, bringing device-independent security closer to real-world deployment.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent definitions of work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for all coarse-grainings, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust while quantities are context-dependent.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum thermodynamics and quantum information by highlighting the role of observation in defining thermodynamic quantities, offering a new perspective on the foundations of thermodynamics in quantum systems.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory. This work aims to test whether entropy can serve as an internal time variable.
method: The authors use an ultracold atomic gas as a mini-universe, monitoring entropy exchange between different sectors of the system to define an internal time.
result: They demonstrate that entropy exchange robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution, showing time can be defined without an external clock.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can emerge from thermodynamic entropy exchange, linking information thermodynamics to fundamental physics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical processes in quantum theory, with implications for identifying resources for quantum technologies.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum and classical processes.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures and shows that many phenomena considered classical actually have intrinsic quantum features.
conclusion: The work refines our understanding of quantumness and may guide the discovery of new quantum resources.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn cavity dissipation, typically a nuisance, into a tool for generating and protecting multipartite entanglement.
method: They propose a hybrid system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity mode. By engineering the dissipation (e.g., via cavity loss and drive), they create a dissipative steady state that is entangled. The reconfigurability comes from tuning experimental parameters like detunings and drive strengths.
result: They show that the steady state can be tuned to exhibit different types of entanglement, including spin-squeezed states and topological states. They also demonstrate enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: Dissipative entanglement engineering in hybrid spin-cavity systems is a powerful and scalable approach for quantum sensing and many-body state preparation, with potential applications in quantum networks and metrology.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss at breakeven using continuous drives, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback. They demonstrate the scheme on a bosonic qubit encoded in a superconducting cavity.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, meaning the error-corrected qubit lives longer than the best unprotected qubit in the same system.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction can achieve breakeven, showing that continuous drives alone can provide effective protection against photon loss, which is a major step toward practical quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, revealing scaling laws of quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information survives under continuous monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size in certain regimes, and identify phase transitions between different scaling behaviors.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum computers.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging spin-photon interfaces and cavity coupling.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with overhead scaling favorably for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using hybrid spin-photon systems, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions and kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phases, such as quantum scars and blockaded superradiance.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg atoms, analyzing the interplay of cavity-mediated long-range interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phases in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg arrays provides a versatile platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum correlations.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications

tldr: This paper introduces a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes and optimized asymmetric geometries to improve quantum repeater performance and resource efficiency.

method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation of quantum tree-codes and explore asymmetric code geometries to reduce resource overhead while maintaining loss tolerance.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher key rates and lower resource requirements compared to symmetric designs, making quantum repeaters more feasible with current technology.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs significantly enhance the practicality of quantum repeaters, advancing the goal of scalable quantum networks.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.

method: The authors develop a general framework that combines device characterization data (e.g., from calibration) with the entropy accumulation theorem to produce composable security proofs that account for device imperfections.

conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical QKD implementations, enabling more efficient and certifiable quantum key distribution.

tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, using quantum information methods to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on quantum information theory, particularly entanglement generation, and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments for gravitationally induced entanglement.
result: It provides a comprehensive status of theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for detecting gravitationally induced entanglement, showing feasibility with current or near-future technology.
conclusion: Quantum information methods offer a promising path to test the quantum nature of gravity, with several feasible experiments that could constrain future theories.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale to macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To unify mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, providing a consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem and provides thermodynamically consistent models for systems far from equilibrium.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, from chemical networks to electronic circuits.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control of a qubit manipulates its environment, demonstrated with superconducting and semiconducting qubit examples.
motivation: Standard quantum reservoir engineering uses a structured environment as an entropy sink, but active control can unlock new functionalities by allowing the system to manipulate its environment.
method: Develops a theoretical framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrates with two physical platforms: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: Qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, showing that repeated initialization of the qubit can manipulate the environment, enabling new open-system functionalities.
conclusion: Active reservoir engineering provides a versatile tool for quantum control and information processing, with potential applications in quantum error correction and entanglement generation.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: This paper transforms the SDP for joint measurability and steering into a hierarchy of linear programs, enabling efficient computation of incompatibility robustness for large measurement sets.
motivation: The standard SDP for deciding joint measurability and steering scales exponentially with the number of measurements, making it intractable for large sets. The authors aim to provide a more efficient method.
method: They convert the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on incompatibility robustness, with polynomial complexity in the number of measurements. The hierarchy converges and applies to arbitrary POVMs.
result: For qubits, the method reliably bounds incompatibility robustness for hundreds of measurements quickly on a laptop. For qutrits, it provides non-trivial bounds where SDP is intractable. It also constructs local hidden state models or certifies steering for two-qubit states.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy offers a practical tool for analyzing measurement incompatibility and quantum steering in large measurement scenarios, outperforming standard SDP approaches in scalability.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: Tight bounds on the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice, including nearly matching lower bounds and a resolution of an open problem in unitary recurrence.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine, but its cost with limited advice (e.g., copies of an eigenstate or a state with known overlap) was not tightly characterized.
method: The authors develop algorithms and prove nearly matching lower bounds using a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, along with reductions from the unitary recurrence problem.
result: They show that small advice is not significantly better than none, and large advice does not reduce cost much; they also tightly bound the cost of error-probability reduction in basic phase estimation.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of phase estimation complexity under various advice models, with implications for quantum algorithms and complexity theory.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: Extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, deriving thermodynamic and fluctuation relations for a strongly coupled quantum particle.
motivation: To understand quantum thermodynamics beyond the weak-coupling and equilibrium reservoir assumptions, and to model engineered reservoirs that can act as work sources.
method: Introduces squeezed and displaced thermal reservoirs, treats them via a modified Keldysh contour, and computes full heat statistics and fluctuation theorems.
result: Shows that strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs generate effective time-dependent Hamiltonians, break fluctuation-dissipation relations, and yield a fluctuation theorem for energy balance.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile framework for non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, with classical correspondence in the heat statistics and trajectory-level energy conservation in the classical limit.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to construct device-independent sequential quantum protocols from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols, ensuring secure correlations.
motivation: Sequential scenarios can enhance device-independent protocols by reusing quantum states, but a general construction method was lacking.
method: Replace one projective measurement in a bipartite self-testing protocol with a non-projective measurement and add an extra user, then prove security via the impossibility of reproducing correlations as a statistical mixture.
result: The constructed ideal correlations are secure, enabling device-independent certification of all randomness in the observed correlations.
conclusion: The recipe provides a general framework for developing new device-independent quantum security schemes in sequential scenarios.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise without non-local classical computation.
motivation: Open problem: whether a local topological quantum memory exists below four dimensions. Prior decoders required non-local classical processing or communication.
method: Uses ideas from hierarchical classical cellular automata (Tsirelson and Gács) to design a strictly local quantum circuit decoder for the 2D toric code.
result: The decoder achieves exponential memory lifetime under circuit-level noise, and can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes.
conclusion: Solves the open problem, demonstrating that local topological quantum memory is possible in 2D (or 3D with time-translation invariance).

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: The paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable bounds on contraction coefficients with applications to quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients give strong data-processing inequalities, but a quantum generalization was lacking. The authors aim to define quantum Doeblin coefficients with desirable properties and interpret them in terms of entanglement and state exclusion.
method: Several quantum Doeblin coefficients are defined, one of which is multiplicative and efficiently computable. They are interpreted as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations, using both entanglement-assisted and unassisted settings.
result: The quantum Doeblin coefficients provide upper bounds on trace-distance contraction coefficients, leading to improved bounds on noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation, sample complexity of hypothesis testing, and mixing times.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for analyzing quantum channels, offering computational efficiency and broad applicability across quantum information processing tasks.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series measurements using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: To learn thermodynamic properties of small systems from experimental data without prior knowledge of the underlying dynamics.
method: The authors use correlation functions and trajectory-fluctuation currents to infer entropy production, free energy differences, and other thermodynamic quantities from time-series data.
result: They demonstrate that thermodynamic quantities can be accurately estimated from correlation and fluctuation currents, validated on simulated systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical framework for extracting thermodynamic information from complex dynamical systems using only observable data.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and for characterizing entanglement phases in monitored circuits.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decoding thresholds and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions corresponding to entanglement phase transitions.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and have implications for quantum error correction and quantum information processing.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates requires extensive doping, establishing a fundamental resource bound.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and for delineating the power of Clifford circuits.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates (e.g., T gates) required for a circuit to approximate random unitaries, using techniques from quantum information theory and representation theory.
result: They show that the non-Clifford cost scales extensively with the number of qubits, meaning that a constant fraction of gates must be non-Clifford to achieve pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The results highlight a fundamental limitation of Clifford circuits and provide guidance for designing efficient pseudorandom unitary generators.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity of stabilizer states, showing maximal violation by states with maximal Wigner negativity.
motivation: Generalize Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems where qubit results do not directly extend, and explore the role of Wigner negativity in nonlocality.
method: Introduces a new CHSH inequality for qudits using correlations derived from Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under a generalized π/8 gate; analyzes Bell operator as a measure of singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
result: A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality, and the Bell operator quantifies Wigner negativity; also shows bipartite entangled qudit states with Wigner negativity witness contextuality.
conclusion: Wigner negativity is a key resource for nonlocality in qudit systems, and the proposed inequality provides a practical tool for detecting nonlocality in higher dimensions.

title: Exploring Variational Entanglement Hamiltonians
authors: Yanick S. Kind And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2133 (2026).

Recent advances in analog and digital quantum-simulation platforms have enabled exploration of the spectrum of entanglement Hamiltonians via variational algorithms. In this work we analyze the convergence properties of the variationally obtained solutions and compare them to numerically exact calculations in quantum critical systems. We demonstrate that interpreting the cost functional as an integral permits the deployment of iterative quadrature schemes, thereby reducing the required number of measurements by more than an order of magnitude even in the presence of noise. We further show that a modified ansatz captures deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models, improves convergence, improves trainability and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Finally, we establish that a low cost value does not by itself guarantee convergence in trace distance. Nevertheless, it faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps, which are essential for applications to topological phases.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes variational algorithms for learning entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum critical systems, improving convergence and measurement efficiency.
motivation: Understanding entanglement Hamiltonians is crucial for characterizing quantum phases, but direct measurement is challenging; variational methods offer a practical alternative.
method: The authors interpret the cost functional as an integral to apply iterative quadrature schemes, and introduce a modified ansatz to capture deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form.
result: The approach reduces required measurements by over an order of magnitude, improves trainability, and provides a diagnostic for quantum phase transitions, though low cost does not guarantee trace distance convergence.
conclusion: Variational entanglement Hamiltonians are a viable tool for studying quantum critical and topological phases, with practical improvements for near-term quantum simulators.

title: Deterministic, Dynamically Reconfigurable Single Quantum Emitters Enabled By Tip-enhanced Nano-optical Trapping Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: Tip-enhanced nano-optical trapping spectroscopy enables deterministic trapping and dynamic control of single quantum emitters, with reversible switching between weak and strong coupling regimes.
motivation: Controlling single quantum emitters with high precision is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing methods lack deterministic trapping and dynamic reconfigurability.
method: The authors use tip-enhanced nano-optical trapping spectroscopy to trap and manipulate single quantum emitters, enabling reversible switching between weak and strong light-matter coupling.
result: They demonstrate deterministic trapping and dynamic control of single emitters, including the ability to switch coupling regimes on demand.
conclusion: This technique provides a versatile platform for studying and exploiting light-matter interactions at the single-emitter level, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Long-lived Photon Blockade With Weak Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates long-lived photon blockade using weak optical nonlinearity in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong nonlinearities; this work aims to achieve it with weak nonlinearities for practical quantum devices.
method: Uses a cavity coupled to a nonlinear medium with engineered dissipation to enhance blockade duration.
result: Achieves photon blockade with significantly extended lifetime compared to conventional schemes.
conclusion: Weak nonlinearities can be sufficient for photon blockade, enabling new quantum optical devices.

title: Three-outcome Multipartite Bell Inequalities: Applications To Dimension Witnessing And Spin-nematic Squeezing In Many-body Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: Derives three-outcome multipartite Bell inequalities and applies them to dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop Bell inequalities beyond the standard two-outcome case for better detection of nonlocality and entanglement in many-body systems.
method: Constructs Bell inequalities using three-outcome measurements and analyzes their violation in spin-nematic squeezed states and other multipartite quantum states.
result: The inequalities provide tighter bounds for dimension witnessing and can detect spin-nematic squeezing, a form of quantum correlations relevant for metrology.
conclusion: Three-outcome Bell inequalities are a useful tool for characterizing quantum correlations in many-body systems and have practical applications in quantum information.

title: High-quality And Field Resilient Microwave Resonators On Ge Quantum Well Heterostructures
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates high-quality, field-resilient microwave resonators on germanium quantum well heterostructures for spin qubit readout.
motivation: Germanium quantum wells host high-mobility holes with strong spin-orbit coupling, promising for fast, all-electrical spin qubits; however, integrating high-quality microwave resonators for readout remains challenging.
method: Fabricated superconducting microwave resonators (NbTiN) on Ge/SiGe heterostructures and characterized their internal quality factors and resilience to magnetic fields up to 1 T.
result: Achieved internal quality factors exceeding 10^5 at low temperatures and maintained high Q-factors under in-plane magnetic fields up to 1 T, demonstrating field resilience.
conclusion: The resonators are suitable for dispersive readout of Ge hole spin qubits, advancing hybrid quantum systems based on Ge quantum wells.

title: Nonstabilizerness And Error Resilience In Noisy Quantum Circuits
authors: Fabian Ballar Trigueros And José Antonio Marín Guzmán
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Ballar Trigueros and José Antonio Marín Guzmán

We investigate how noise impacts nonstabilizerness—a key resource for quantum advantage—in many-body qubit systems. While noise typically degrades quantum resources, we show that amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably ca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240602] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how noise affects nonstabilizerness (magic) in many-body qubit systems, finding that amplitude damping can generate or enhance it while depolarizing noise cannot.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its behavior under noise is poorly understood; understanding this is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the effect of amplitude damping and depolarizing noise on nonstabilizerness in many-body qubit systems, likely using stabilizer formalism and resource measures.
result: Amplitude damping, a nonunital channel, can generate or enhance nonstabilizerness, whereas depolarizing noise provably cannot.
conclusion: Noise is not always detrimental to quantum resources; certain nonunital channels can actually boost nonstabilizerness, which has implications for error resilience and quantum advantage.

title: Theory Of Quantum Comb Enhanced Interferometry
abstract:
Author(s): Haowei Shi and Quntao Zhuang

Optical frequency combs, named for their comblike peaks in the spectrum, are essential for various sensing applications. As the technology develops, its performance has reached the standard quantum limit dictated by the quantum fluctuations of coherent light field. Quantum combs, with their quantum …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243602] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of quantum comb enhanced interferometry, showing how quantum combs can surpass the standard quantum limit for phase estimation.
motivation: Optical frequency combs are essential for sensing but are limited by the standard quantum limit; quantum combs offer a path to enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors propose a theoretical framework for quantum combs—multimode squeezed states with comb-like frequency structure—and analyze their application to interferometric phase estimation using quantum Fisher information and error analysis.
result: Quantum combs can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in phase sensitivity, outperforming classical combs and conventional squeezed states.
conclusion: Quantum comb interferometry provides a practical route to surpass the standard quantum limit in frequency comb-based sensing, with potential applications in precision metrology.

title: Compensating Random Transition-Detection Blackouts In Markov Networks
authors: Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, And Udo Seifert
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, and Udo Seifert

In Markov networks, measurement blackouts with unknown frequency compromise observations such that thermodynamic quantities can no longer be inferred reliably. In particular, the observed currents neither discern equilibrium from nonequilibrium nor can they be used in extant estimators of entropy pr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 247101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper addresses how to infer thermodynamic quantities from Markov networks when random measurement blackouts occur, proposing a method to compensate for missing data.
motivation: Measurement blackouts in Markov networks compromise the inference of thermodynamic quantities like entropy production, making it impossible to distinguish equilibrium from nonequilibrium or use standard estimators.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to correct for random transition-detection blackouts, likely using statistical inference or information-theoretic techniques to recover reliable estimates from incomplete observations.
result: They demonstrate that their compensation method allows accurate inference of thermodynamic currents and entropy production even under random blackouts, restoring the ability to detect nonequilibrium behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing experimental data from Markov networks with missing observations, extending the applicability of thermodynamic inference methods.

title: Entanglement Transition In Unitary System-Bath Dynamics
authors: Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, And Dario Poletti
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, and Dario Poletti

The evolution of a system coupled to baths is commonly described by a master equation that, in the long-time limit, yields a steady-state density matrix. However, when the same evolution is unraveled into quantum trajectories, it is possible to observe a transition in the scaling of entanglement wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240401] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Unraveling a system-bath master equation into quantum trajectories reveals a transition in the scaling of entanglement with system size.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement behaves in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors study unitary system-bath dynamics via quantum trajectories, analyzing entanglement scaling across different unravelings.
result: They observe a transition in entanglement scaling from area-law to volume-law as a function of measurement strength or bath coupling.
