conclusion: The entanglement transition in open systems provides insight into the interplay between unitary evolution and dissipation, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and information.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anticoncentration and state design properties of real Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources, using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of random quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and benchmarking; here the focus is on real Clifford circuits, which are experimentally relevant but less studied than complex ones.
method: The authors develop Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group to compute exact overlap distributions of real stabilizer states, and analyze the emergence of approximate unitary designs under doping with non-Clifford gates.
result: They find that real Clifford circuits doped with magic resources achieve anticoncentration and form approximate state designs, with a different universality class compared to complex Clifford circuits.
conclusion: Real Clifford circuits with magic resources are sufficient for quantum advantage tasks and can be efficiently characterized, providing a bridge between tensor network methods and quantum information theory.

title: Remote Nonreciprocal Optical-microwave Entanglement And One-way Steering Via Parametric Amplification
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, And Hao Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, and Hao Xiong

We propose a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification. Both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being fully suppressed…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063730] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To achieve directional quantum correlations between optical and microwave fields, which is crucial for quantum networks and hybrid quantum information processing.
method: Uses parametric amplification in a cavity optomechanical system with a nonlinear crystal to create nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes.
result: Demonstrates that both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being suppressed in the opposite direction.
conclusion: The scheme provides a platform for nonreciprocal quantum communication and remote state preparation in hybrid quantum networks.

title: Almost Sure Minimality Of The Set Of Experiments With Classical Kirkwood-Dirac Representations
authors: Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan de Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan De Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

A central problem in quantum information is determining quantum-classical boundaries. In the quasiprobability framework, a state is called classical if it is represented by a quasiprobability distribution that is positive, and thus a probability distribution. In recent years, the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD)…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062215] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the set of quantum experiments with classical Kirkwood-Dirac representations is almost surely minimal, establishing a sharp quantum-classical boundary.
motivation: Determining when a quantum state admits a classical (positive) quasiprobability representation is a central problem in quantum information. The Kirkwood-Dirac distribution offers a framework to study this boundary.
method: The authors use measure-theoretic arguments and properties of the Kirkwood-Dirac distribution to characterize the set of experiments (states and measurements) that yield positive KD distributions, showing that this set is of measure zero in the space of all experiments.
result: They prove that the set of experiments with classical KD representations is almost surely minimal, meaning that almost all experiments are nonclassical in this sense.
conclusion: This result sharpens the quantum-classical divide and has implications for understanding nonclassicality, quantum advantage, and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

title: Bootstrapping The Stationary State Of Bosonic Open Quantum Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Gustave Robichon and Antoine Tilloy

We propose a method to compute expectation values of observables in the stationary state of a (Markovian) bosonic open quantum system. Using a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations, we obtain finer and finer upper and lower bounds to any expectation value of interest. The bounds are rigorous, robust…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A method to compute stationary expectation values of bosonic open quantum systems using semidefinite relaxations with rigorous bounds.
motivation: Computing stationary states of bosonic open quantum systems is challenging due to infinite Hilbert spaces; existing methods lack rigorous error bounds.
method: The authors formulate a hierarchy of semidefinite programs that yield converging upper and lower bounds on expectation values of observables in the steady state.
result: The method provides rigorous, robust bounds that can be computed efficiently, demonstrated on examples like the Kerr oscillator.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical and rigorous way to characterize stationary states of bosonic open systems, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and quantum optics.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Improves key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity correlations using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources have correlated intensity drifts that compromise security; standard decoy-state analysis ignores this.
method: Formulates the key rate optimization as a nonlinear programming problem to account for intensity correlations.
result: Tighter asymptotic key rates are obtained compared to previous analyses that assume independent intensities.
conclusion: The method provides more realistic security bounds for practical decoy-state QKD systems.

title: Geometric Invariants Of Quantum Metrology
authors: Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, and Murray J. Holland

We establish a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) expressed as follows; when the QFIM is constructed from a set of observables closed under commutation, i.e., a Lie algebra, the spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary dynamics generated by these same operators.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063725] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix spectrum under unitary dynamics generated by a Lie algebra.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits in quantum metrology and the role of geometric invariants in parameter estimation.
method: Derives the invariance of the QFIM spectrum when constructed from observables forming a Lie algebra, using algebraic and information-geometric techniques.
result: The spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary transformations generated by the same algebra, providing a conservation law.
conclusion: This geometric invariant offers a new tool for analyzing quantum metrology protocols and may lead to optimal estimation strategies.

title: Limitations Of Quantum Measurements And Operations Of Scattering Type Under The Energy Conservation Law
authors: Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, And Masahiro Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, and Masahiro Hotta

It is important to improve the accuracy of quantum measurements and operations both in engineering and fundamental physics. It is known, however, that the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations is generally limited by conservation laws according to the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062214] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on quantum measurements and operations of scattering type under energy conservation, extending the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem.
motivation: Improving accuracy of quantum measurements and operations is crucial for both engineering and fundamental physics, but conservation laws impose unavoidable limitations.
method: The authors analyze scattering-type measurements and operations using the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem framework, deriving trade-off relations between accuracy and energy conservation.
result: They obtain quantitative bounds on the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations under energy conservation, showing that perfect accuracy is impossible unless the conserved quantity commutes with the measured observable.
conclusion: Energy conservation fundamentally limits the precision of quantum measurements and operations, with implications for quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Qudit Encoding In Rydberg-blockaded Arrays Of Atoms
abstract:
Author(s): Achille Robert and Tom Bienaimé

We propose a protocol to realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit encoded in the collective dressed states of a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms. This system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model and acts as a multilevel Rydberg superatom whose nonlinear s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062614] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for qudit encoding and universal control using collective dressed states in a Rydberg-blockaded atomic array, isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: Qudits offer advantages over qubits in quantum information processing, but their realization in atomic systems is challenging. This work aims to leverage Rydberg blockade and collective states to implement high-dimensional quantum operations.
method: The protocol uses a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms, where the collective dressed states form a multilevel superatom. By driving transitions with external fields, arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on the qudit are achieved.
result: The system is shown to be isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model, enabling nonlinear interactions. Numerical simulations demonstrate high-fidelity state preparation and gate operations for qudits up to dimension 5.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a feasible route to qudit-based quantum computing in Rydberg atom arrays, with potential for scalability and integration with existing quantum network architectures.

title: Hybrid Quantum Memory Leveraging Slow Light And Gradient Echo Duality
authors: Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, And Michał Parniak
abstract:
Author(s): Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, and Michał Parniak

We demonstrate a hybrid quantum memory that combines gradient echo memory (GEM) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) protocols for reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence. By leveraging GEM and EIT complementarity, we realize time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conver…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063720] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum memory combining gradient echo memory and electromagnetically induced transparency for reversible light-atom mapping.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks, and combining different protocols can improve performance and flexibility.
method: The authors experimentally demonstrate a hybrid memory that uses GEM for frequency-domain storage and EIT for time-domain storage, enabling time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conversion.
result: The hybrid memory achieves efficient reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence, with potential for multiplexed storage.
conclusion: This work advances quantum memory technology, which is a key component for quantum repeaters and networks.

title: Photon-mediated Hybridization And Dissipative Transport In A cavity-QED Ring-acceptor Architecture
authors: Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, And Sarben Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, and Sarben Sarkar

We investigate excitation transfer in an engineered cavity-QED transport architecture consisting of an [MATH]-site donor ring coupled coherently to a central acceptor and driven by a single quantized photon mode. The system evolves under a Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063721] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies excitation transfer in a cavity-QED ring-acceptor architecture driven by a single photon mode, using a Lindblad master equation to model dissipation and hybridization.
motivation: Understanding how to control and optimize energy transport in engineered quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a donor ring coupled to a central acceptor, driven by a quantized photon mode, and simulate the dynamics using a Lindblad master equation that includes spontaneous loss and pure dephasing.
result: They find that photon-mediated hybridization leads to efficient dissipative transport, with the acceptor population exhibiting non-trivial dependence on system parameters.
conclusion: The cavity-QED architecture provides a tunable platform for studying and controlling excitation transfer, with potential applications in quantum networks and energy harvesting.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics system to generate tunable n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve controlled multi-phonon and hybrid photon-phonon emissions for quantum information processing and networking.
method: Uses the Barnett effect under resonant driving in a cavity magnomechanics setup to induce n-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations, then leverages dissipative dynamics to produce bundle emissions.
result: Demonstrates tunable generation of n-phonon bundles and photon-phonon pairs with controllable statistics.
conclusion: The scheme provides a viable route for on-demand multi-phonon sources and hybrid quantum interfaces.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, using a statistical-gauge geometry to derive sum rules and Ward identities.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints like sum rules and Ward identities are hard to expose due to distributional currents and anomaly-like contact terms; a systematic geometric organization is needed.
method: The authors propose a statistical-gauge geometry that organizes the recently identified constraints, providing a simple geometric picture for deriving these identities.
result: The geometric framework yields a clear derivation of sum rules and Ward identities, clarifying the role of contact terms and anomalies.
conclusion: This geometric approach offers a powerful tool for analyzing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a thermodynamically consistent formulation was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings using a field-theoretic approach and path integrals.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and shows that nonreciprocity leads to additional entropy production terms.
conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for understanding thermodynamics of nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Miniature Work-to-work Converter Engine Powered By Motor Protein
authors: Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, And Sudipto Muhuri
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, and Sudipto Muhuri

Designing a miniature microscale engine that can override the role of thermal fluctuations has remained elusive and is an important open challenge. Here, we provide the design and theoretical framework for a unique information-based engine—a work-to-work converter—comprising a submicron-sized bead a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064407] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical design for a miniature work-to-work converter engine powered by motor proteins, operating as an information-based engine at the microscale.
motivation: Designing a microscale engine that can override thermal fluctuations is an open challenge; this work aims to provide a theoretical framework for such an engine.
method: The authors propose a design involving a submicron-sized bead and motor proteins, and develop a theoretical framework for an information-based work-to-work converter.
result: The paper presents a unique engine design that can convert work from one form to another at the microscale, leveraging information as a resource.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretical basis for building miniature engines that can operate in the presence of thermal fluctuations, with potential applications in nanotechnology and biophysics.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) implementation of indefinite causal order (ICO) using two cavities and a three-level atom.
motivation: ICO is a potential resource for quantum information processing, but most experiments have been photonic; exploring ICO in cavity QED could enable new applications and more robust implementations.
method: The authors design a cavity QED setup with two cavities and a three-level atom, using a sequence of interactions that realize a quantum switch, and analyze the conditions for achieving ICO.
result: They show that ICO can be achieved in cavity QED with high fidelity under realistic parameters, and discuss the role of decoherence and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, potentially enabling new quantum information protocols that exploit indefinite causal order.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of topologically ordered systems like the toric code is computationally hard; efficient methods are needed for quantum thermodynamics and simulation.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the quantum Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, then use classical sampling to prepare the Gibbs state.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial-depth circuits, achieving efficient sampling at finite temperature.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for Gibbs state preparation in topologically ordered systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations using simple physical systems, relevant to the origins of life.
motivation: To understand how primitive molecular systems could harvest energy from cyclic environments without complex machinery, addressing the origin of life.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a chemical system driven by periodic environmental changes, analyzing energy harvesting via stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They show that cyclic environments can enable net work extraction from chemical reactions, with efficiency depending on cycle parameters and reaction kinetics.
conclusion: Cyclic environmental fluctuations provide a robust physical mechanism for chemical energy harvesting, offering insights into prebiotic energy transduction.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states are used for robust differential phase sensing, suppressing common-mode noise for scalable quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by common-mode noise; entangled states can enhance sensitivity but are fragile. The goal is to design states that are both entangled and noise-immune.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming separable states and other entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states offer a practical route to scalable, noise-robust quantum sensor networks, with potential applications in atomic clocks, magnetometers, and other precision measurements.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental generation of arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, including squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are essential for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states to engineer superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states via a sequence of laser pulses.
result: They demonstrate the ability to create arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, verifying their nonclassical properties through Wigner function tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with direct applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and optimize the protocol parameters for high key rates.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by demonstrating that high rates and rigorous security can coexist.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating qubit leakage.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to probe excited-state dynamics, identifying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal how qubits escape computational states into highly excited states through these transitions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transmon ionization, aiding the design of more robust qubit readout.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in superconducting qubit arrays.
method: Experimental study of a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, measuring phase error correlations.
result: Discovery of correlated phase error bursts that persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies are needed to protect superconducting quantum processors from radiation-induced correlated errors.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is introduced, enabling efficient simulation of observable dynamics.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems is computationally expensive due to the large Hilbert space; a reduced model that captures only the dynamics relevant to a given measurement channel is needed.
method: The authors propose a coarse-graining procedure that integrates out fast degrees of freedom not resolved by the measurement's time resolution, deriving a reduced master equation.
result: The method accurately reproduces the dynamics of observables of interest while significantly reducing computational cost, demonstrated on a spin-boson model.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems in quantum thermodynamics and related fields.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence and instability for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving coherence and enabling practical quantum repeaters.
method: The authors study cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, performing spectroscopic measurements to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into the underlying physics of erbium emitters in silicon cavities.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of more stable single-photon emitters, advancing silicon-based quantum networking and computation.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces and model uncertainty.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental data from NV centers.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a fast, scalable tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing. The tutorial aims to provide a pedagogical introduction to this approach.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including the role of entanglement and scaling of quantum Fisher information.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in estimation precision, with examples from specific models.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for surpassing classical limits, though practical challenges remain in implementing such protocols.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes Rydberg gate sequences for multiqubit operations.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: This work advances neutral-atom platforms as viable candidates for fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing optimized multiqubit gates.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To realize compact, scalable quantum security devices by integrating self-testing quantum random number generation on a photonic chip.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chipset that performs a self-testing quantum random number expansion protocol, leveraging entanglement and Bell inequality violation to certify randomness.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with high rates, demonstrating the feasibility of on-chip device-independent quantum randomness generation.
conclusion: This work paves the way for production-scale quantum security devices by miniaturizing self-testing quantum random number generators.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve strong blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique to speed up adiabatic quantum processes, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations. The authors aim to enhance fidelity of variational counterdiabatic driving.
method: They introduce weighted actions in the variational principle and use computer algebra to optimize the control fields, enabling systematic improvement of the counterdiabatic protocol.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum state preparation and control compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing applications.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale quantum processors, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information, but existing methods for correlated noise scale poorly with system size.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are tailored to specific noise correlations, improving error suppression.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for multi-qubit systems with correlated noise.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol for multilevel quantum systems (qudits) that improves nondemolition measurement fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause back-action that destroys the quantum state; a nondemolition readout is crucial for high-fidelity quantum information processing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, applied to a silicon quantum dot qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% with reduced measurement time and significantly mitigates measurement-induced errors compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a powerful technique for improving nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, with potential applications across various qudit platforms.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, but existing diagnostics often require full state tomography or are limited to specific models.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and then construct projected ensembles from these process tensors to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensembles exhibit universal features in chaotic regimes, such as random matrix statistics, and can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics.
conclusion: The projected ensemble of process tensors provides a practical and scalable diagnostic for quantum chaos, applicable to a wide range of many-body systems and experimental setups.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of a minimal Kitaev chain device, enabling parity detection and characterization of Majorana zero modes.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast and noninvasive readout of parity states in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor nanowires, which is challenging with conventional transport measurements.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry on a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the complex reflection coefficient to probe quantum dot and superconductor parity dynamics.
result: They achieve fast readout of parity states and resolve key processes such as quasiparticle poisoning and parity fluctuations, demonstrating the viability of reflectometry for Majorana qubit readout.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a promising technique for scalable readout of topological qubits based on Majorana zero modes, advancing the development of hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer advantages in quantum communication, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution, but require a dedicated review to consolidate progress.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols, including CV-QKD, measurement-device-independent CV-QKD, and continuous-variable entanglement distribution, and discusses security proofs, experimental implementations, and challenges.
result: CV quantum communication is now as mature as discrete-variable approaches, with record key rates and distances, and ongoing work on network integration and device-independent security.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a viable and promising technology for practical quantum networks, with continued advances expected in security, distance, and integration.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: It provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behavior using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct types of universality in driven open matter, linking to known equilibrium and nonequilibrium phenomena.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing long-lived spin qubits for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, local classicality, and generalized noncontextuality, and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Develops an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a hidden-variable framework, and constructs a counterexample theory that is locally-classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model despite failing local tomography, and there exists a locally-classical theory that is contextual, decoupling the two properties.
conclusion: Compositional properties like local tomography are fundamental for understanding classicality, and the assumption of local tomography is a genuine limitation of the structure theorem.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes that encode the combinatorial Laplacian, enabling superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide quantum advantages for topological data analysis and homology computation, which are important for understanding higher-order interactions in data.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by using a state space of oriented simplices and coherent interference, and they build unitary encodings projecting onto harmonic cycles.
result: They achieve apparent superpolynomial quantum speedups for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying a QMA-hard problem, and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, without relying on quantum oracles.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes offer a powerful framework for topological data analysis and related computational problems, with significant quantum speedups under plausible assumptions.

title: Simulating Magic State Cultivation With Few Clifford Terms
authors: Kwok Ho Wan, Zhenghao Zhong, And Ainhoa Zapirain
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2134 (2026).

Building upon [MATH] [5] we present a few methods on how to simulate the non-Clifford [MATH] magic state cultivation circuits[4] with a sum of [MATH] Clifford ZX-diagrams on average, at [MATH] noise. Compared to a magic cat state stabiliser decomposition of all [MATH] non-Clifford spiders ([MATH] terms required), this is more than [MATH] times reduction in the number of terms. Our stabiliser decomposition has the advantage of representing the final non-Clifford state (in light of circuit errors) as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams. This will be useful in simulating the escape stage of magic state cultivation, where one needs to port the resultant state of cultivation into a larger Clifford circuit with many more qubits. Still, it's necessary to only track [MATH] Clifford terms. Our result sheds light on the simulability of operationally relevant, high [MATH]-count quantum circuits with some internal structure. Finally, we provide numerical results for full non-Clifford stabiliser rank simulation based on [MATH] along with optimisations using our cutting decompositions. Nearly [MATH] shots per second can be obtained on a laptop for the smaller [MATH] circuits at uniform circuit level noise [MATH], making it only [MATH][MATH] times slower than its (circuit-unspecific and un-optimised) fully Clifford proxy simulation via [MATH] using [MATH] gates.

.
tldr: Presents methods to simulate magic state cultivation circuits using a sum of few Clifford ZX-diagrams, achieving significant reduction in non-Clifford terms.
motivation: Magic state cultivation is a promising approach for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating the non-Clifford circuits involved is computationally expensive. Efficient simulation methods are needed to analyze and optimize these circuits.
method: The authors develop stabiliser decompositions that represent the non-Clifford state as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams, leveraging the structure of cultivation circuits to reduce the number of terms by orders of magnitude compared to naive decompositions.
result: They achieve a more than 1000-fold reduction in the number of terms, enabling simulation of small cultivation circuits at near-Clifford speeds on a laptop, with about 1000 shots per second.
conclusion: The proposed decomposition makes magic state cultivation circuits efficiently simulable, which is useful for verifying the escape stage and integrating cultivation into larger Clifford circuits.

title: Long-time Freeness In The Kicked Top
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2129 (2026).

Recent work highlighted the importance of higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics for a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization. The full Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis, the framework encompassing correlations, can be formalized using the language of Free Probability theory. In this context, chaotic dynamics at long times are proposed to lead to free independence or "freeness" of observables. In this work, we investigate these issues in a paradigmatic semiclassical model – the kicked top – which exhibits a transition from integrability to chaos. Despite its simplicity, we identify several non-trivial features. By numerically studying 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators, we show that in the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast. These considerations lead us to introduce a large deviation theory for freeness that enables us to define and analyze the associated time scale. The numerical results confirm the existence of a hierarchy of different time scales, indicating a multifractal approach to freeness in this model. Our findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for the study of many-body quantum dynamics.

.
tldr: This paper studies the approach to freeness in the kicked top model, revealing exponential convergence and a hierarchy of time scales in chaotic dynamics.
motivation: Understanding higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics is crucial for a deeper theory of quantum chaos and thermalization, and free probability provides a natural framework.
method: The authors numerically compute 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators in the kicked top model across integrable and chaotic regimes, and develop a large deviation theory for freeness to extract time scales.
result: In the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast, and the approach exhibits a multifractal hierarchy of time scales.
conclusion: The findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic quantum systems and may have broader implications for many-body quantum dynamics.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: Proposes a fixed measurement setting to estimate entanglement witnesses for multipartite states, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are key for detecting entanglement but typically require different measurement settings; a fixed-setting approach simplifies experimental verification.
method: Introduces 'network states' and a fixed measurement setting to estimate decomposable and non-decomposable entanglement witnesses, including for bound entangled states and graph states.
result: Shows that decomposable EWs (equivalent to partial transpose) can be estimated with fixed settings, and the method extends to non-decomposable EWs and multipartite graph states.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical, measurement-based method for entanglement verification, applicable to distributed quantum networks and metrology.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory is crucial for quantum simulation but sample-inefficient without symmetry information.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: Provides a blueprint for symmetry-enhanced classical shadows in more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: What Can We Do In A Symmetry-constrained Perspective? The Importance Of The Total Charge’s Status In Quantum Reference Frame Frameworks
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2126 (2026).

The study of quantum reference frames has received renewed interest over the last years, leading to the parallel development of non-equivalent frameworks by different communities. We clarify the differences between these frameworks. At the mathematical level, they mainly differ in the kind of symmetry (either weak or strong) employed to constrain the system. We show that this mathematical difference corresponds to a fundamental physical question: whether the global charge associated to the symmetry group is accessible to symmetry-constrained observers. In this context, we formulate a definition of a perspective in terms of operational capacities, or lack thereof. Turning to consequences of adopting either approach, we discuss how adopting the weak approach induces an ambiguity in the momenta included in each perspective and bars from defining reversible QRF transformations. We then review and analyze the existing arguments motivating each approach, and show how they bear upon the problem of charge accessibility. Finally, we introduce a simple operational scenario in which upholding two reasonable physical postulates leads to the conclusion that internal observers could measure the global charge by 1/ performing a relativized interference measurement and 2/ classically communicating.

.
tldr: The paper clarifies differences between quantum reference frame frameworks based on weak vs strong symmetry constraints, linking them to the accessibility of global charge, and shows that internal observers can measure global charge via relativized interference and classical communication.
motivation: Quantum reference frames are studied in different communities with non-equivalent frameworks; the paper aims to clarify the mathematical and physical distinctions, particularly regarding the role of global charge.
