While they have demonstrated considerable promise in solving problems of practical interest, efficiently determining the minimal quantum resources necessary to obtain such a solution remains an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062617] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of overparametrization in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), showing that overparametrization can improve convergence and reduce quantum resources.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA require careful tuning of circuit depth and parameters; understanding overparametrization could help minimize quantum resources while maintaining performance.
method: The authors analyze QAOA analytically and numerically, examining how increasing the number of parameters (overparametrization) affects the optimization landscape and convergence to the optimal solution.
result: Overparametrization in QAOA leads to faster convergence and can reduce the required circuit depth, but the benefits saturate beyond a certain point.
conclusion: Overparametrization is a useful technique for improving QAOA performance, but its benefits are limited and must be balanced against increased computational cost.

title: Unveiling Distinguishable non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, And Andrea Conti
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, and Andrea Conti

Quantum systems promise unprecedented performance with respect to classical counterparts for various applications involving sensing, communications, control, and computing. Bringing this promise to reality hinges upon the distinguishability between quantum states. This paper explores the distinguish…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062435] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores distinguishability of non-Gaussian quantum states, focusing on a theoretical framework for quantifying state discrimination.
motivation: Quantum state distinguishability is crucial for quantum sensing, communication, and computing; non-Gaussian states offer advantages but are less studied.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on quantum state discrimination theory, possibly using fidelity or other distance measures tailored to non-Gaussian states.
result: They identify conditions under which non-Gaussian states are more distinguishable than Gaussian ones, providing bounds or criteria for distinguishability.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian states can enhance distinguishability in certain regimes, with implications for quantum information tasks.

title: Entanglement Dynamics For Atoms Near A Reflecting Boundary: Enhancement And Suppression By Environment-induced Interactions
authors: Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, And Jiawei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, and Jiawei Hu

We investigate how environment-induced interactions influence the entanglement dynamics of two atoms held at fixed positions near a perfectly reflecting boundary. Within the framework of open quantum systems, we explicitly incorporate the environment-induced energy shifts, including both atom-bounda…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how environment-induced interactions affect entanglement dynamics of two atoms near a reflecting boundary.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in open quantum systems is important for quantum information processing, but the focus here is on environmental effects rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects.
method: Using an open quantum systems framework, the authors incorporate environment-induced energy shifts and derive master equations for two atoms near a reflecting boundary.
result: They find that environment-induced interactions can either enhance or suppress entanglement depending on interatomic distances and boundary conditions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling entanglement via environmental engineering, but does not directly address thermodynamic or information-theoretic constraints.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improving VQE ansatz design for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices.
method: Starts with an approximate multiqubit target state and uses quantum information measures to construct an efficient ansatz.
result: Demonstrates efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems.
conclusion: The ansatz is efficient and accurate for atomic systems, potentially useful for quantum chemistry simulations.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes fermionic nonstabilizerness (magic) measures for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates using exact diagonalization or tensor network methods.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in the binding-energy curve for H2 and other dimers.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary quantum-information-theoretic insight into molecular bonding, highlighting a new resource beyond entanglement.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide systematic optimization.
method: Defines new control parameters beyond stellar rank and uses them to design and optimize optical circuits for state generation.
result: Achieves orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The proposed control parameters enable scalable and efficient generation of non-Gaussian states, advancing quantum information applications.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for characterizing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of topological order, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of quantum LDPC codes with high encoding rate, and demonstrates constant-depth magic state distillation protocols.
result: Achieves high-fidelity magic state generation with reduced overhead compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing by lowering the cost of magic states.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying where quantum advantage may arise.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than information-theoretic or cryptographic applications.
method: Uses complexity theory to analyze parameter regimes of matrix functions, likely employing reductions and oracle models.
result: Provides a complexity classification that delineates regimes where quantum algorithms outperform classical ones.
conclusion: Offers insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but the contribution is primarily computational complexity, not directly aligned with core quantum information topics.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is hard, but for small patches of the landscape, efficient surrogates may exist, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical machine learning.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values for nearby points, reducing the need for quantum resources.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical way to enhance classical simulation of quantum circuits, particularly for variational algorithms.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
result: Demonstrates accurate prediction of Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth for driven quantum systems.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum dynamics.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana bound states.
conclusion: The work establishes practical measures for Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Abelian braiding.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The simulation becomes scalable and efficient for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols.
conclusion: The proposed technique enables practical classical simulation of magic state preparation, which is important for verifying fault-tolerant quantum computing schemes.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes that are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, enabling single-shot correction.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common patterns of assumption violation and shows how designed materials can exploit these to achieve properties beyond classical bounds.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but stem from misapplied assumptions; this insight can guide development of advanced materials.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: Analytical study of dynamical Lie algebras for QAOA circuits, focusing on barren plateaus and DLA dimensions for cycle and complete graphs.
motivation: Understanding barren plateaus is crucial for training variational quantum algorithms; DLA provides a theoretical tool to analyze trainability.
method: The authors analytically compute DLA dimensions and structures for general graphs, then derive explicit bases and decompositions for cycle and complete graphs.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a center and semisimple part, proving absence of barren plateaus; for complete graphs, DLA dimension is n^2.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous analytical results on QAOA trainability via DLA, but the focus on combinatorial optimization and variational algorithms is not a core interest.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: Proposes an efficient classical algorithm to compute the Neural Tangent Kernel of Clifford+Pauli quantum neural networks, showing they cannot achieve quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether wide quantum neural networks can outperform classical computers, by leveraging the NTK framework and Gaussian process equivalence.
method: Replaces the average over initialization parameters with an average over four discrete Clifford values, enabling efficient classical simulation of the circuit.
result: The algorithm computes the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks classically, proving no quantum advantage for this class.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks with Clifford+Pauli structure are classically simulable and cannot provide a quantum speedup.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: This paper uses tensor cross interpolation to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (set of bipartite Rényi entropies) of quantum many-body states, demonstrating polynomial sample complexity for states with matrix product state structure.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical learning has been unexplored.
method: The authors apply the tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state, using polynomial samples in system size.
result: TCI successfully learns entanglement features for Haar random states, random MPS, and certain eigenstates of 1D quantum systems, with sample complexity scaling polynomially.
conclusion: The learned entanglement feature enables tasks like quantifying distance between entanglement patterns and finding optimal 1D ordering of indices, showing potential for many-body entanglement analysis.

title: Quantum Mechanics Based On Real Numbers: A Consistent Description
authors: Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, And Dagmar Bruß
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, and Dagmar Bruß

By exploiting a physically motivated principle, rather than a mathematical postulate, researchers offer a new perspective on how a real-valued quantum theory can be constructed.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240202] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a consistent real-valued quantum theory based on a physically motivated principle rather than a mathematical postulate.
motivation: Standard quantum mechanics uses complex numbers, but real-valued formulations have been proposed; the authors aim to provide a physically consistent real-valued theory.
method: They exploit a physically motivated principle to derive a real-valued quantum theory, ensuring consistency with physical predictions.
result: A consistent description of quantum mechanics using only real numbers is achieved, matching empirical predictions.
conclusion: Real-valued quantum mechanics can be a viable alternative to complex-valued quantum mechanics, with implications for foundations and potential computational advantages.

title: Quantum Non-Gaussianity Criterion Based On Photon Correlations ${g}^{(2)}$ And ${g}^{(3)}$
authors: Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

Quantum non-Gaussian states, which cannot be written as mixtures of Gaussian states, are necessary to achieve a quantum advantage in continuous variable systems. They represent an important benchmark for the realization of an advanced quantum light source, as they cannot be made by simple means such…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a criterion for quantum non-Gaussianity based on second- and third-order photon correlations.
motivation: Quantum non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but existing criteria are limited; a simpler correlation-based criterion is needed.
method: Derives necessary and sufficient conditions for quantum non-Gaussianity using g^(2) and g^(3) correlation functions, and tests them on experimental data from a quantum dot single-photon source.
result: The criterion successfully identifies quantum non-Gaussian states and is robust to experimental imperfections, outperforming previous criteria in certain regimes.
conclusion: The g^(2)-g^(3) criterion provides a practical tool for certifying quantum non-Gaussian light sources, advancing quantum optics and continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Microwave-free Vector Magnetic-field Measurement Using A Single Nitrogen-vacancy-center Spin In Diamond
authors: Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, And Lumin Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, and Lumin Ji

Magnetic field sensors based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have attracted considerable attention due to their high sensitivity and spatial resolution. However, conventional vector magnetometry typically relies on either the four axes of ensemble NV centers or three orthogonal reference magnetic f…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062618] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A microwave-free vector magnetometry method using a single NV center in diamond is demonstrated.
motivation: Conventional NV-based vector magnetometry requires microwave fields or multiple NV axes, which can be limiting; a simpler, microwave-free approach using a single NV center is desired.
method: The method exploits the spin-dependent fluorescence of a single NV center under static magnetic fields, using a sequence of optical and static magnetic field pulses to reconstruct the vector field without microwaves.
result: The technique achieves vector magnetic field measurement with high sensitivity and spatial resolution using only a single NV center.
conclusion: This work provides a simplified approach to vector magnetometry that avoids microwave hardware, potentially enabling more compact and robust sensors.

title: Evolution Of Quantum State Texture Under Lorentz Transformations: Invariance, Competition, And Sensitivity In Single-particle And Bipartite Entangled Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiming Huang

Quantum state texture (QST), an emerging resource quantifying the global structural complexity of quantum states within a computational basis, exhibits dynamical behavior under relativistic frameworks that remains largely unexplored. This paper systematically investigates the evolution of QST under …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how quantum state texture (a measure of structural complexity) evolves under Lorentz transformations for single-particle and bipartite entangled states.
motivation: To understand the relativistic behavior of a newly proposed quantum resource, quantum state texture, which quantifies global structural complexity.
method: Analytical calculations of quantum state texture under Lorentz boosts for single-qubit and two-qubit states, including maximally entangled and Werner states.
result: Quantum state texture is not Lorentz invariant; it shows competition between texture components and sensitivity to boost parameters and entanglement.
conclusion: Quantum state texture is a frame-dependent quantity, and its evolution under Lorentz transformations reveals nontrivial interplay with entanglement.

title: Krylov-space Anatomy And Spread Complexity Of A Disordered Quantum Spin Chain
authors: Bikram Pain, David E. Logan, And Sthitadhi Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Bikram Pain, David E. Logan, and Sthitadhi Roy

We investigate the anatomy and complexity of quantum states in Krylov space, in the ergodic and many-body localized (MBL) phases of a disordered, interacting spin chain. The Krylov basis generated by the Hamiltonian from an initial state provides a representation in which the spread of the time-evol…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214205] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Krylov-space anatomy and spread complexity of quantum states in a disordered spin chain across ergodic and many-body localized phases.
motivation: Understanding the structure of quantum states in Krylov space can reveal signatures of ergodicity and localization, which are central to quantum thermalization and information scrambling.
method: The authors construct the Krylov basis from the Hamiltonian and an initial state, then analyze the spread complexity and other measures of state complexity in the ergodic and MBL phases.
result: They find that spread complexity distinguishes ergodic from MBL phases, with ergodic phases showing higher complexity and faster growth, while MBL phases exhibit suppressed complexity.
conclusion: Krylov-space analysis provides a useful diagnostic for many-body localization and quantum thermalization, but the paper does not directly address thermodynamic or information-theoretic constraints.

title: Exact Multivalley Envelope Function Theory Of Valley Splitting In Si/SiGe Nanostructures
authors: Lasse Ermoneit, Abel Thayil, Thomas Koprucki, And Markus Kantner
abstract:
Author(s): Lasse Ermoneit, Abel Thayil, Thomas Koprucki, and Markus Kantner

Valley splitting in strained Si/SiGe quantum wells is a central parameter for silicon spin qubits and is commonly described with envelope function and effective mass theories. These models provide a computationally efficient continuum description and agree well with atomistic approaches when the con…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops an exact multivalley envelope function theory for valley splitting in Si/SiGe quantum wells, relevant for silicon spin qubits.
motivation: Valley splitting is a key parameter for silicon spin qubits, and accurate modeling is needed to understand and optimize qubit performance.
method: The authors derive an exact envelope function theory that accounts for multivalley effects and compare it with effective mass and atomistic approaches.
result: The theory provides a computationally efficient continuum description that agrees well with atomistic simulations for typical quantum well parameters.
conclusion: The exact multivalley envelope function theory offers a reliable tool for designing Si/SiGe quantum wells for spin qubits, bridging continuum and atomistic models.

title: Magnon Diffusion Length And Longitudinal Spin Seebeck Effect In Vanadium Tetracyanoethylene $\mathrm{V}{[\mathrm{TCNE}]}_{x}$ $(x∼2)$
authors: Seth W. Kurfman, Denis R. Candido, Brandi Wooten, Yuanhua Zheng, Michael J. Newburger, Shuyu Cheng, Roland K. Kawakami, Joseph P. Heremans, Michael E. Flatté, And Ezekiel Johnston-Halperin
abstract:
Author(s): Seth W. Kurfman, Denis R. Candido, Brandi Wooten, Yuanhua Zheng, Michael J. Newburger, Shuyu Cheng, Roland K. Kawakami, Joseph P. Heremans, Michael E. Flatté, and Ezekiel Johnston-Halperin

The study of spin-thermal processes is limited by the small number of magnetic materials where these effects are easily distinguished and the limited regimes wherein the theory is tractable. This paper incorporates the temperature dependence of magnon nonconserving processes, demonstrating quantitative agreement with established data sets and leading to the prediction of a high‑efficiency regime defined by low‑magnetization, ultra‑low‑damping magnetic materials. This prediction is validated in the organic ferrimagnetic semiconductor V[TCNE]
[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220408] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon diffusion and the longitudinal spin Seebeck effect in the organic ferrimagnet V[TCNE]x, predicting a high-efficiency regime for spin-thermal effects.
motivation: To understand spin-thermal processes in magnetic materials and identify regimes where these effects are large and tractable.
method: The authors incorporate temperature dependence of magnon nonconserving processes into a theoretical model and validate it against experimental data from V[TCNE]x.
result: They find quantitative agreement with established data and predict a high-efficiency regime in low-magnetization, ultra-low-damping materials, confirmed in V[TCNE]x.
conclusion: V[TCNE]x exhibits spin-thermal effects comparable to yttrium iron garnet, offering a new platform for spin caloritronics.

title: Breakdown Of Bosonic Thouless Pump Due To Interaction In A Quasiperiodic Lattice
authors: Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, And Ulrich Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, and Ulrich Schneider

Remarkably, even weak interactions cause of a breakdown of the quantized Thouless pump in a bosonic quasicrystal, despite its known robustness against disorder. Sharp jumps in the transport as a function of interaction strength are traced back to the closing of specific doublon channels. Most strikingly, repulsive doublons – two bosons occupying the same site – survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher ones, draining energy from the driven system rather than heating it.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235131] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Weak interactions cause breakdown of quantized Thouless pumping in a bosonic quasicrystal due to doublon dynamics.
motivation: Thouless pumping is robust against disorder but its stability under interactions is unclear; understanding this is important for transport in interacting topological systems.
method: Numerical simulations of bosons in a quasiperiodic lattice with interactions, analyzing doublon formation and transport.
result: Interactions cause sharp jumps in transport due to closing of doublon channels; repulsive doublons survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher bands.
conclusion: Interactions can destroy quantized pumping even in systems robust to disorder, highlighting the role of doublon dynamics.

title: Quantum Hyperuniformity And Quantum Weight
abstract:
Author(s): Junmo Jeon and Shiro Sakai

Extending hyperuniformity from classical to quantum fluctuations in electron systems yields a framework that identifies quantum phase transitions and reveals underlying gap structures through the quantum weight. We study long-wavelength fluctuations of many-body ground states through the charge-dens…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241113] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Extends hyperuniformity to quantum fluctuations in electron systems, linking quantum weight to phase transitions and gap structures.
motivation: To develop a framework for identifying quantum phase transitions and understanding gap structures via long-wavelength fluctuations.
method: Analyzes charge-density fluctuations in many-body ground states using the concept of quantum weight.
result: Establishes a connection between quantum hyperuniformity and quantum weight, revealing signatures of phase transitions.
conclusion: Quantum hyperuniformity provides a new tool for probing quantum phase transitions and electronic structure.

title: Vanishing Correlations In Stochastic And Bistochastic Controlled Circuits
authors: Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, and Tomaž Prosen

We study the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates. This type of dynamics arises from quantum circuits with random controlled gates, as well as in stochastic circuits and deterministic classical cellular automata. We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding correlation decay in controlled circuits is important for characterizing the dynamics of quantum and stochastic systems.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates, proving that correlations vanish after a finite number of steps.
result: They show that for such circuits, the correlation functions become zero beyond a certain range, independent of the system size.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous understanding of correlation decay in a broad class of controlled circuits, with applications to quantum information and statistical mechanics.

title: Exact Steady States And Fragmentation-induced Relaxation In The No-passing Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
abstract:
Author(s): Urei Miura

We introduce a multispecies generalization of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with a “no-passing” constraint, forbidding overtaking, on a one-dimensional reflecting (closed) chain without particle reservoirs. This no-passing rule fragments the Hilbert space into an exponential number of disj…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064129] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A multispecies asymmetric simple exclusion process with a no-passing constraint is studied, revealing Hilbert space fragmentation and exact steady states.
motivation: To understand relaxation dynamics and fragmentation in constrained classical stochastic systems, which may inform quantum many-body physics.
method: The paper introduces a no-passing rule in a multispecies ASEP on a closed chain, analyzes the fragmented Hilbert space, and derives exact steady states using matrix product states or combinatorial methods.
result: The Hilbert space fragments into exponentially many sectors, each with its own steady state, leading to non-ergodic relaxation and slow dynamics.
conclusion: The no-passing constraint induces strong fragmentation, providing a classical analog to quantum many-body scarring and Hilbert space fragmentation.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
motivation: Understanding resetting processes in underdamped systems is important for stochastic thermodynamics and control of small systems, but the paper focuses on classical stochastic processes rather than quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Analytical and numerical methods are used to solve the underdamped Langevin equation with resetting, computing position and velocity distributions and correlation functions.
result: The two resetting protocols lead to different steady-state distributions and relaxation times, with the Maxwell-distributed velocity resetting yielding a non-equilibrium steady state with non-zero average velocity.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed characterization of resetting in underdamped Brownian motion, but does not directly address quantum thermodynamics or information processing constraints.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases, proposing a tunable intertwined phase accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To explore out-of-equilibrium phases arising from driven collective excitations in systems with enlarged symmetry manifolds.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven symmetry-broken phases, deriving the driven phase diagram and identifying conditions for intertwined phases.
result: A tunable intertwined phase is predicted, which can be realized in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experiments.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new route to engineer out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases via periodic driving, with experimental feasibility.

title: Optical Spin Pumping In Silicon
authors: Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, And Fabio Pezzoli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, and Fabio Pezzoli

The optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population is a keystone process for quantum technologies and spintronics alike. Although this is an established technique for studying direct band-gap semiconductors, it has been proven limited in materials that possess weak oscillator strengths …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023302] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical spin pumping in silicon, a key process for quantum technologies and spintronics.
motivation: Optical spin pumping is established in direct band-gap semiconductors but limited in materials with weak oscillator strengths like silicon; the authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors use optical excitation and spin-dependent recombination to generate an out-of-equilibrium spin population in silicon, characterized by photoluminescence and spin transport measurements.
result: They achieve efficient optical spin pumping in silicon, demonstrating a viable method for spin initialization in this indirect band-gap material.
conclusion: The work establishes silicon as a platform for optical spin control, relevant for quantum technologies and spintronics.

title: Macroscopic Localization And Collective Memory In Poisson Renewal Resetting
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Vilk

Stochastic renewal processes are ubiquitous across physics, biology, and the social sciences. Here, we show that continuous-time renewal dynamics can naturally produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure, with a macroscopic fraction of particles occupying a discrete state. For ensembles of continu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023305] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous-time renewal processes can exhibit macroscopic localization and collective memory, forming a mixed discrete-continuous structure.
motivation: Stochastic renewal processes are common in many fields, and understanding their emergent collective behavior is important for modeling systems with memory and resetting.
method: The author analyzes continuous-time renewal dynamics analytically and numerically, demonstrating that a macroscopic fraction of particles can occupy a discrete state, leading to a mixed structure.
result: The dynamics produce a macroscopic localized state with collective memory, characterized by a non-trivial stationary distribution and long-term correlations.
conclusion: Renewal resetting can naturally generate macroscopic localization and memory, which may have implications for understanding non-equilibrium systems and information storage in stochastic processes.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field regimes for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: A specular ray-tracing algorithm is employed to analyze thermal equilibrium and heat transfer in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Violation of Kirchhoff's law leads to monochromatic thermal currents and directional heat transfer in the far-field.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable novel thermal management and circuitry applications, but the work is primarily applied and not deeply connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting Bell states in high-energy photon pairs where standard polarization analysis is difficult due to the need for Compton scattering.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and define polarization symmetry as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles.
result: They prove that polarization symmetry holds if and only if the initial two-photon state is a Bell state, and demonstrate the method's feasibility with simulated data.
conclusion: Polarization symmetry provides a robust experimental signature for Bell states, enabling entanglement certification in Compton scattering experiments without full state tomography.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena unique to open quantum systems far from equilibrium, specifically in periodically driven-dissipative systems.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional driven-dissipative chain using the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation, focusing on the Liouvillian spectrum and topological invariants.
result: They identify topological phases characterized by winding numbers and show nonreciprocal dynamics, including directional amplification and edge modes.
conclusion: The work reveals that open Floquet systems can host topological features without equilibrium counterparts, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation, a phase transition, could enable cells to process high-dimensional information, linking phase transitions to computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, and phase transitions offer a physical mechanism for information processing that is fundamentally different from traditional molecular signaling.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and discusses how phase separation can implement computations like sensing, classification, and response, drawing analogies to neural networks and statistical physics.
result: It proposes that phase transitions in biomolecular condensates can perform high-dimensional information processing, potentially more efficiently than molecular networks.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for cellular computation, but experimental validation and theoretical development are needed to realize its potential.

method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling simulation of larger circuits.

conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, relevant for verifying quantum devices.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective dynamics for these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel metastable phases.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and control of orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. Temporal coarse-graining is then achieved by conditioning the stochastic process on a coarse realization of the noise, expressing the conditioned stochastic process in terms of a sum of smooth, deterministic functions and bridge processes with boundaries fixed at zero, and performing the ensemble average over the bridge processes. For Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, the deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the stochastic bridge processes are not only independent but taken from the same distribution with correlators that can be expressed analytically, allowing the associated noise propagators to be precomputed once for all simulations. This combination of noise trajectories on a coarse time grid and ensemble averaging over bridge processes has practical advantages, such as a simple concatenation rule, that we highlight with numerical examples.

.
tldr: A method for simulating quantum systems with classical stochastic noise using temporal coarse-graining and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems with noise exhibiting temporal correlations over many time scales (e.g., 1/f noise) is computationally challenging.
method: The noise is expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes; temporal coarse-graining conditions the process on a coarse realization, separating deterministic and bridge components, with the bridge ensemble averaged analytically.
result: The deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and bridge processes are independent with analytically known correlators, enabling precomputation of noise propagators.
conclusion: The approach offers practical advantages like a simple concatenation rule and is demonstrated with numerical examples.

title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: Derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical circuits that provide necessary conditions for exact and approximate state preparation.
motivation: Linear optics without post-selection cannot produce arbitrary quantum states, limiting applications that require entangled resources; understanding the constraints is essential.
method: Identifies conserved quantities from the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians and uses them to derive invariants of the density matrix spectrum.
result: Provides necessary conditions for exact state preparation and a lower bound on the distance between output and target states based on invariant differences.
conclusion: Future state preparation methods must consider these invariants to rule out impossible evolutions, narrowing the search for useful entangled states.

title: Thermomechanics Of Odd Matter: From Deterministic To Stochastic Media
abstract: Odd matter exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive response while remaining compatible with balance laws and the second law of thermodynamics. We develop a unified continuum framework based on Edelen’s primitive thermodynamics, which decomposes generalized forces into gradient (hyperdissipative) and orthogonal (powerless) components. We show that this convex decomposition in velocity space admits an elastic analogue: hyperelastic response corresponds to integrable stresses derived from a stored-energy potential, while odd elasticity arises as the non-integrable, yet not derivable from a stored-energy potential branch of admissible response. Within the odd elasticity, we distinguish two cases: an instantaneous power orthogonality (the stronger one) or a configurational orthogonality (the weaker one). Working within the case of configurational orthogonality we construct the (linear) thermo-poromechanical theory, derive a finite strain odd neo-Hookean solid, and establish preservation of coercivity and exponential energy decay in random fluid and solid odd continua. Scale-dependent homogenization preserves coercivity of the even part and orthogonality of the odd part. In driven granular Couette flow, odd stresses modify fluctuation statistics without producing entropy, consistent with the fluctuation theorem. The results provide a systematic thermodynamic foundation for odd matter in deterministic and stochastic settings.
tldr: Develops a thermodynamic framework for odd matter using Edelen's primitive thermodynamics, showing odd elasticity as non-integrable but admissible response.
motivation: Odd matter exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive behavior that must be reconciled with thermodynamics; a unified continuum framework is needed.
method: Applies convex decomposition of generalized forces into gradient and orthogonal components, and constructs linear and finite-strain odd elastic theories.
result: Odd stresses in driven granular Couette flow modify fluctuation statistics without entropy production, consistent with the fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic thermodynamic foundation for odd matter, preserving coercivity and orthogonality in random media.

title: Dynamics Of A Tracer Trapped In A Correlated Medium In The Presence Of A Wall
authors: Marcin Piotr Pruszczyk And Andrea Gambassi
abstract: We describe the random motion of a particle immersed in a thermally fluctuating medium and harmonically trapped at a certain distance from a wall. The medium, modeled by a Gaussian field with a tunable correlation length , is linearly coupled to the particle and evolves according to dissipative relaxational dynamics. Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on the field at the wall give rise to a repulsive fluctuation-induced force acting on the particle, causing a shift in its average position and a renormalization of the strength of the harmonic trap. We describe the effective overdamped dynamics of the particle, which features a nonlinear memory term depending on the wall-particle separation. We show that the two-time correlation function of the particle position features a memory-induced term that depends on the distance of the particle from the wall. At the critical point, this term decays algebraically upon increasing time and it displays a crossover from the behavior observed in the bulk to that corresponding to having the particle at the wall. Our results establish a concrete connection between boundary-induced modifications of critical fluctuations and the non-equilibrium, memory-dependent dynamics of a trapped particle.
tldr: A theoretical study of a tracer particle trapped near a wall in a correlated fluctuating medium, showing how boundary-induced critical fluctuations lead to non-equilibrium memory effects in the particle's dynamics.
motivation: To understand how a wall (boundary) modifies the fluctuation-induced forces and dynamics of a particle in a correlated medium, bridging critical phenomena and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The medium is modeled as a Gaussian field with relaxational dynamics and Dirichlet boundary conditions at the wall; the particle is harmonically trapped and linearly coupled to the field. The effective overdamped dynamics of the particle is derived, including a nonlinear memory term.
result: The two-time correlation function of the particle position shows a memory-induced term that depends on wall distance; at the critical point, this term decays algebraically with a crossover from bulk to wall behavior.
conclusion: The work establishes a concrete connection between boundary-modified critical fluctuations and non-equilibrium, memory-dependent dynamics of a trapped particle, relevant to soft matter and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Nonequilibrium Dimension-raising Phase Transitions
abstract: We propose a periodically driven system whose dimensionality is an emergent property that can be tunable, thus enables us to realize not only many-body phases with arbitrary dimensions, but also phase transitions, instead of crossovers, between phases with various dimensions. We study an interacting rotor model whose instantaneous Hamiltonian keeps the one-dimensional feature at any given time. Despite this, an emergent two-dimensional (2D) phase appears when the driving frequency exceeds a critical value, at which a dimension-raising phase transition takes place. We find that the nonequilibrium feature of the system could qualitatively change the finite temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase and make it different from its equilibrium counterpart. A four-dimensional generalization and experimental realizations of the proposed model based on a programmable reconfiguration technique in optical tweezers setups have also been discussed.
tldr: A periodically driven system exhibits a nonequilibrium phase transition that raises the effective dimensionality, with critical behavior distinct from equilibrium.
motivation: To explore how periodic driving can induce emergent higher-dimensional phases and phase transitions in low-dimensional systems, and to understand the nonequilibrium effects on critical phenomena.
method: The authors study an interacting rotor model with a time-dependent Hamiltonian that remains one-dimensional at any instant, using analytical and numerical methods to analyze the emergence of a two-dimensional phase above a critical driving frequency.
result: A dimension-raising phase transition occurs at a critical driving frequency, and the finite-temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase differs qualitatively from its equilibrium counterpart. A four-dimensional generalization is also discussed.
conclusion: Periodic driving can realize phase transitions between phases of different dimensionality, with nonequilibrium effects altering the critical behavior, offering a new route to engineer higher-dimensional phases in low-dimensional setups.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type memory effects in the orientational relaxation of nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by suppressing slow modes.
motivation: Understanding and overcoming memory effects that limit acceleration of relaxation in stochastic systems with many degrees of freedom.
method: Experimental optical monitoring of field-induced birefringence combined with Smoluchowski equation modeling; polydispersity generates multiscale relaxation.
result: Kovacs nonmonotonic relaxation observed; sequential suppression of slowest modes reduces relaxation time compared to standard protocols.
conclusion: Memory effects from polydispersity can be mitigated by tailored multi-step protocols, providing a strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.

title: Subgap Pumping Of Antiferromagnetic Mott Insulators: Photoexcitation Mechanisms And Applications
authors: Radu Andrei, Mingyao Guo, Mustafa G Ali, Hoon Kim, Richard D Averitt, David Hsieh And Eugene Demler
abstract: We study the behavior of the 2D repulsive Hubbard model on a square lattice at half filling, under strong driving with ac electric fields, by employing a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach. Within the same theoretical framework, we analytically obtain the conventional Keldysh crossover between multiphoton and tunneling photoexcitation mechanisms, as well as two new regimes beyond the Keldysh paradigm. We discuss how dynamical renormalization of the Mott–Hubbard gap feeds back into the photoexcitation process, modulating the carrier generation rate in real time. The momentum distribution of quasiparticle excitations immediately after the drive is calculated, and shown to contain valuable information about the generation mechanism. Finally, we discuss experimental probing of the pump-induced nonequilibrium electronic state.
tldr: This paper studies photoexcitation mechanisms in antiferromagnetic Mott insulators under strong ac driving, revealing regimes beyond the Keldysh crossover and dynamical gap renormalization.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems is important for controlling electronic properties with light.
method: A time-dependent Gaussian variational approach is used to analyze the 2D repulsive Hubbard model at half filling under strong ac electric fields.
result: The authors identify two new photoexcitation regimes beyond the conventional Keldysh crossover and show that dynamical renormalization of the Mott-Hubbard gap modulates carrier generation in real time.
conclusion: The momentum distribution of quasiparticles after the drive contains information about the generation mechanism, and experimental probes are discussed.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed technique significantly reduces the number of T gates required for certain quantum circuits.
conclusion: The work provides a new algebraic tool for T-count reduction, contributing to resource optimization in fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Bosonic Content Of Three-fermion Highest-spin States
authors: Jerzy Cioslowski, Krzysztof Strasburger, And Denis K. Sunko
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2121 (2026).

A rigorous characterization of the information content of any highest-spin three-fermion wave function is presented. It is based upon a formal decomposition of the wave function into a finite set of fixed invariants, called shapes, whose sole purpose is to satisfy the Pauli principle, and a variable part, constituting the bosonic excitations of these invariants, that provides its physical content. As an example, this decomposition is applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of the lowest-energy quartet electronic state of the lithium atom. This wave function, which comprises hundreds of basis functions, is reduced to eleven shape blocks, only five of which are numerically significant. Such a compact characterization is a generic example of the appearance of superselection rules in configuration space, and provides a qualitative aid in the search for robust few-particle entangled states.

.
tldr: This paper decomposes three-fermion highest-spin wave functions into fixed invariants (shapes) and bosonic excitations, applied to the lithium atom.
motivation: To characterize the information content of fermionic wave functions and identify robust few-particle entangled states.
method: Formal decomposition of the wave function into shape invariants satisfying the Pauli principle and a variable bosonic part.
result: A benchmark lithium wave function with hundreds of basis functions is reduced to eleven shape blocks, five of which are numerically significant.
conclusion: The decomposition reveals superselection rules in configuration space and aids in finding robust entangled states.

title: Nonclassical Photocounting Statistics With A Single On-off Detector
authors: V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, And A. A. Semenov
abstract:
Author(s): V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, and A. A. Semenov

Any single on-off photocounter, which can only detect the presence or absence of photons without discriminating their number, is not capable of identifying the nonclassical nature of light. This limitation arises because any photocounting statistics obtained with such a detector can be easily reprod…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063726] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that a single on-off detector cannot certify nonclassical light, but two detectors can, using a witness based on photocounting statistics.
motivation: To determine whether nonclassical photocounting statistics can be identified with minimal resources, specifically a single on-off detector.
method: The authors analyze photocounting statistics from on-off detectors and derive a nonclassicality witness based on the covariance of click counts from two detectors.
result: A single on-off detector cannot distinguish nonclassical from classical statistics, but two detectors can, as demonstrated with experimental data.
conclusion: Two on-off detectors are sufficient to certify nonclassical light, providing a practical tool for quantum optics experiments.
