motivation: Efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity is needed for quantum systems.

result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for spectral analysis.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool for analyzing eigenvalue spectra in quantum systems.

tldr: This paper demonstrates nanoscale strain wave generation using a piezoelectric grating formed by polar vortices, focusing on materials physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To create a tunable diffraction grating for strain waves at the nanoscale, enabling control of lattice dynamics in functional materials.
method: A periodic array of polar vortices in a ferroelectric material is modulated by an electric field to act as a piezoelectric grating, generating coherent strain waves.
result: The grating produces nanoscale strain waves with controllable wavelength and amplitude, characterized by X-ray diffraction.
conclusion: Polar vortex structures can serve as dynamic elements for strain wave manipulation, with potential applications in acousto-optics and nanomechanics.

tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling, revealing anomalous tunneling phenomena.
motivation: To understand the effect of nonlinear coupling on Landau-Zener tunneling, which is a fundamental quantum dynamics problem.
method: Combines analytical calculations and phase-space analysis to study the two-level system with nonlinear coupling.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling strength, the tunneling behavior deviates from the standard Landau-Zener formula, exhibiting anomalous features.
conclusion: The work provides a general theory for nonlinear Landau-Zener tunneling, which may have implications for systems with nonlinear interactions.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich
abstract:
Author(s): Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, and Luca Salasnich

An atomic Josephson junction realized with dipolar bosons in a double-well potential can be described by an extended Bose-Hubbard model in which dipolar interactions generate an effective on-site interaction and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling. Using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization, we i…

tldr: This paper studies equilibrium and dynamical quantum phase transitions in dipolar atomic Josephson junctions using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the effects of dipolar interactions and pair tunneling on quantum phase transitions in a bosonic Josephson junction.
method: The authors employ a mean-field approach and exact diagonalization of an extended Bose-Hubbard model with on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: They identify equilibrium phase transitions and dynamical transitions, showing that dipolar interactions and pair tunneling significantly alter the phase diagram and dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the rich physics of dipolar bosons in double-well potentials, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

abstract:

We investigate the stability of current-carrying states with quasimomentum [MATH] in the Bose-condensed phase of the hard-core Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice, where particles transfer between two sites separated by distance [MATH] with hopping amplitude decaying algebraically with [MATH] as $∝{r}^{−α…

tldr: This paper studies the stability of current-carrying states in hard-core bosons with long-range hopping on a square lattice, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how long-range hopping affects the stability of superfluid currents in a Bose-Hubbard model, which is relevant to transport in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors use mean-field theory and numerical simulations to analyze the decay of current-carrying states as a function of hopping range and interaction strength.
result: They find that long-range hopping can stabilize current-carrying states against decay, with a critical hopping exponent determining stability.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the robustness of persistent currents in lattice bosons, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resurgent Reentrant Localization In A non-Hermitian Quasiperiodic Chain
authors: Haoyu Wang, Fuming Xu, Liantuan Xiao, Suotang Jia, Jun Chen, And Lei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Wang, Fuming Xu, Liantuan Xiao, Suotang Jia, Jun Chen, and Lei Zhang

We investigate localization transitions in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chain with period-2 mosaic modulation and nonreciprocal hopping. We show that tuning the degree of non-Hermiticity can induce a rich reentrant localization behavior: As the hopping asymmetry increases, reentrant…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214204] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The paper reviews the concept of space-time duality in lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and its connection to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems, highlighting exactly solvable models and the analogy with quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuit theory.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that preserve a symmetry, which is a topic in quantum computation theory.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define two topological invariants (anyon permutation and generalized GNVW index) and proves classification theorems.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality cannot be extended to a full QCA.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are classified by anyon permutations and an index, with implications for symmetry-protected topological phases.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement using spin-squeezed states in lossy multi-path atom interferometers, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but losses degrade performance. The authors aim to quantify realistic gains under lossy conditions.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering. One-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated for phase sensitivity.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree yields several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature reduces the benefit.
conclusion: Spin-squeezed states can enhance atom interferometry under realistic losses, but practical challenges like temperature must be addressed to realize the gains.

title: Quantum Phases And Stability Of Bose–Hubbard Triangular Ladder With Magnetic Field
authors: Yue Jian, Jun-Hua Luo, Zi-Fa Yu, Juan Zhang, Ying-Ge Xu And Ju-Kui Xue
abstract: We investigate the ground state properties of interacting bosons on a triangular ladder subject to an artificial magnetic field. By means of the mean-field approximation, rich phases are revealed in the limit of weak interaction and large bosons occupation per site, including the Meissner superfluid, vortex superfluid, biased chiral superfluid (C-SF), C-SF and insulating phases. The quantum phases can be precisely identified and the underlying physics of phase transitions can be clarified by utilizing order parameters based on the atomic density, the effective rung current, and the current asymmetry ratio. Meanwhile, the phase transition of the system can be effectively controlled by adjusting the rung-to-leg coupling ratio, the magnetic flux and the atomic interaction. Furthermore, using Bogoliubov theory, we have mapped the stability phase diagram across all parameters, and clarified the interdependence between superfluidity and the dispersion relation. The excitation spectrum, which effectively describes the system’s energetic stability, is governed by the rung-to-leg coupling ratio, the magnetic flux, and the atomic interaction. Numerical simulations validate the dynamical instability of the system. This work offers a theoretical foundation for identifying new quantum phases exhibited by ultracold atoms in optical lattices and new experimental approaches for achieving system superfluidity.
tldr: This paper studies ground state phases and stability of a Bose-Hubbard triangular ladder in a magnetic field using mean-field and Bogoliubov theory.
motivation: To understand quantum phases and phase transitions in ultracold bosons on a triangular ladder under an artificial magnetic field.
method: Mean-field approximation to obtain phase diagrams and Bogoliubov theory to analyze excitation spectra and dynamical stability.
result: Identifies Meissner superfluid, vortex superfluid, biased chiral superfluid, chiral superfluid, and insulating phases; maps stability phase diagram.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for identifying new quantum phases and achieving superfluidity in ultracold atom experiments.

title: Symmetry-induced Logarithmic Relaxation In The Quantum Kicked Rotor
authors: Julien Hébraud, Floriane Arrouas, Bruno Peaudecerf, Juliette Billy, David Guéry-Odelin, Olivier Giraud, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié And Christian Miniatura
abstract: We study the effect of discrete symmetries on coherent multiple scattering in the quantum kicked rotor. When the initial momentum is set to zero—as in recent Bose–Einstein condensate experiments—the effective pseudo-disorder becomes even under momentum inversion. The resulting discrete mirror symmetry of the dynamics profoundly alters spectral correlations: it generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets localised at opposite momenta, whose exponentially small splittings produce a hierarchy of exponentially large dynamical timescales. The coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks then exhibit a striking non-monotonic evolution and strongly asymmetric contrasts, followed by an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation toward a common asymptotic value—a hallmark of glassy dynamics, here emerging in a fully coherent quantum system. That such archetypal glass-like behaviour arises from a single discrete symmetry constraint reveals an unexpected and deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation phenomena.
tldr: This paper shows that discrete mirror symmetry in the quantum kicked rotor leads to logarithmic relaxation, a glassy dynamics signature, in a fully coherent quantum system.
motivation: To understand how discrete symmetries affect coherent multiple scattering and spectral correlations in quantum systems, and to explore the emergence of slow relaxation without disorder.
method: The authors study the quantum kicked rotor with zero initial momentum, analyze Floquet quasi-energy spectra, and compute coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks using numerical simulations and symmetry arguments.
result: Mirror symmetry creates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets with exponentially small splittings, leading to non-monotonic evolution of scattering peaks and an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation to a common asymptotic value.
conclusion: A single discrete symmetry can induce glassy dynamics in a coherent quantum system, revealing a deep connection between symmetry and slow relaxation.

method: Adapts the microcanonical framework of equilibrium statistical mechanics using an ergodic prescription.
result: Computes the wave spectrum at any location in the domain.
conclusion: The equilibrium statistical mechanics approach can be extended to inhomogeneous moving media for wave statistics.

method: First-principles DFT, constrained RPA, and dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) calculations.
result: Identified specific adatom configurations that yield massless Dirac fermions and flat bands with strong correlations.
conclusion: These systems are promising for studying correlated topological phases and Mott physics.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246902] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals a superconducting Berry curvature dipole, linking superconductivity to Bloch band Berry curvature responses.
motivation: To explore the interplay between superconductivity and Berry curvature effects in Bloch bands.
method: Theoretical analysis combining superconducting order with Berry curvature dipole formalism.
result: Discovery of a superconducting Berry curvature dipole that arises from the interplay of Cooper pairs and band geometry.
conclusion: This work establishes a new class of nonlinear responses in superconductors driven by Berry curvature.

tldr: The paper generalizes the Kramers-Wannier duality to study unconventional gapped phases of qudit spin chains using a bilinear phase map.
motivation: To explore a broader spectrum of generalized quantum phases beyond conventional dualities.
method: Introduces a bilinear phase map encoded as a matrix that generalizes the Kramers-Wannier transformation for qudit spin chains.
result: The bilinear phase map enables the investigation of unconventional gapped phases in qudit systems.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for studying quantum phases in spin chains, extending known duality transformations.

motivation: Understanding finite-size effects in coupled oscillator systems is important for realistic modeling, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive explicit expressions for the covariance function of fluctuations of the complex order parameter using a mean-field approximation.
result: They obtain the variance of the order parameter magnitude entirely from the system's parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for finite-size fluctuations in classical synchronization, but has no direct relevance to the user's research interests.

motivation: To understand the relationship between conformal manifolds and exactly marginal operators in conformal field theories.
method: The authors assume the existence of a conformal interface connecting nearby CFTs and use it to construct an exactly marginal operator.
result: They show that under the given assumptions, an exactly marginal operator exists that connects the CFTs.
conclusion: The work provides a general proof that conformal manifolds imply exactly marginal operators, deepening the understanding of CFT moduli spaces.

title: Probing Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer Pairing And Quasiparticle Formation In Ultracold Gases By Rydberg Atom Spectroscopy
authors: Emilio Ramos Rodríguez, Marcel Gievers, And Richard Schmidt

Locally probing pairing in fermionic superfluids, ranging from micro- to macroscopic scales, has been a long-standing challenge. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243401] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using Rydberg impurities as a spectroscopic probe to study Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer pairing and quasiparticle formation in ultracold Fermi gases.
motivation: Locally probing pairing in fermionic superfluids across scales has been challenging; a new spectroscopic method is needed.
method: The authors theoretically investigate a Rydberg impurity embedded in an ultracold Fermi gas, using its spectroscopic response to infer properties of the paired fermions.
result: The Rydberg atom spectroscopy can reveal signatures of BCS pairing and quasiparticle formation, providing a local probe of the superfluid state.
conclusion: Rydberg impurities offer a viable tool for spatially resolved spectroscopy of fermionic superfluids, enabling studies of pairing from micro to macroscopic scales.

title: Repulsive-Interaction-Driven Topological Superconductivity In A Landau Level Coupled To An $s$-Wave Superconductor

tldr: This paper studies topological superconductivity in a Landau level coupled to an s-wave superconductor, driven by repulsive interactions.
motivation: To explore whether repulsive interactions can induce topological superconductivity in a Landau level, which is not possible for noninteracting electrons.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and likely numerical methods to study the interplay of Landau levels, proximity-induced pairing, and repulsive interactions.
result: They find that repulsive interactions can drive a topological superconducting phase in a Landau level proximity-coupled to an s-wave superconductor.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new mechanism for topological superconductivity, expanding the possibilities for realizing such states in quantum Hall systems.

title: High-contrast Bragg Atom Interferometer For Testing Continuous Spontaneous Localization
authors: Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, And Minkang Zhou

The continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model is one of the most promising approaches to address the wave-function collapse problem in the measurement process of standard quantum mechanics. In this work, the effect of the CSL model on a Bragg atom interferometer is investigated. A Bragg interf…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the effect of the continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model on a Bragg atom interferometer, proposing a high-contrast setup to test wave-function collapse.
motivation: The CSL model addresses the wave-function collapse problem, and atom interferometry offers a sensitive testbed for collapse models.
method: The authors analyze the impact of CSL on a Bragg atom interferometer, deriving the decoherence effect and optimizing parameters for high contrast.
result: They find that the CSL-induced decoherence can be detected with high-contrast interferometry under realistic conditions.
conclusion: The proposed Bragg atom interferometer can serve as a sensitive test of the CSL model, potentially ruling out certain parameter regimes.

title: Dual-state Control Of Lasing And Absorption Via Conjugate Exceptional Points
authors: Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, And Lin Wu
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063521] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a unified scattering framework for controlling lasing and absorption in a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity using conjugate exceptional points.
motivation: To achieve coordinated control of lasing and absorption in a single photonic device, enabling multifunctional applications.
method: The authors design a Fabry–Pérot microcavity with tailored gain and loss to support conjugate exceptional points, and analyze the scattering properties using non-Hermitian topology.
result: The system exhibits frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption, with state switching enabled by the exceptional points.
conclusion: This work opens new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices that can simultaneously act as lasers and absorbers.

title: Coherent Control Of The Goos-Hänchen Shift In Polariton Optomechanics
abstract:

We propose a theoretical scheme for controlling the Goos-Hänchen shift (GHS) of a reflected probe field in a polariton optomechanical system. tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical scheme to control the Goos-Hänchen shift in a polariton optomechanical system, which is a classical optical phenomenon with no clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To achieve coherent control of the Goos-Hänchen shift using a hybrid polariton optomechanical system, potentially for sensing or switching applications.
method: The system couples an optical cavity mode, molecular vibrations, and excitonic modes via conditional displacement, and the Goos-Hänchen shift of a reflected probe field is analyzed using input-output formalism.
result: The Goos-Hänchen shift can be controlled by adjusting system parameters such as coupling strengths and detunings.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to manipulate the Goos-Hänchen shift in a hybrid quantum system, but the work is primarily classical optics and does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments.
motivation: To demonstrate the application of quantum annealing for computing molecular properties, specifically electric dipole moments.
method: Quantum annealing is used to simulate molecular Hamiltonians; dipole moments are extracted via finite-field method by applying an electric field perturbation and measuring energy responses.
result: The computed dipole moments for several molecules are presented, showing agreement with known values.
conclusion: Quantum annealing can be a viable tool for computing molecular properties, though the approach is still in early stages.

title: Optimally Driving Multiphoton Transitions In The Perturbative Single-mode Regime
authors: Frieder Lindel, Stefan Yoshi Buhmann, Andreas Buchleitner, And Edoardo G. Carnio

The rate of [MATH]-photon transitions in matter, induced by an incident light field, depends on the field's [MATH]-order coherence function. Consequently, the coherence properties of the light field may be shaped to increase the rate of multiphoton transitions. Here, we determine the optimal st…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063727] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper optimizes the coherence properties of light fields to enhance multiphoton transition rates in the perturbative single-mode regime.
motivation: Multiphoton transitions are important for spectroscopy and quantum control, and their rates depend on the coherence of the driving field. The authors aim to find the optimal field statistics to maximize these rates.
method: Using a perturbative approach, they derive the transition rate as a function of the field's nth-order coherence function and then optimize over all possible classical and quantum states of the field.
result: They find that the optimal field is a Fock state with exactly n photons, which maximizes the nth-order coherence function and thus the transition rate.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limit on multiphoton transition rates and suggests that non-classical light can significantly enhance multiphoton processes.

method: Uses plane-wave solutions in Rindler coordinates to model the scalar field and computes transition rates or entanglement properties.
result: Quantifies the effect of acceleration on atom-field interactions and mirror dynamics.
conclusion: Provides insights into Unruh-like effects and quantum information in accelerated systems.

motivation: To understand the properties of a two-component BEC in the presence of altermagnetic order, which breaks spin-rotation symmetry but has zero net magnetization.
method: Bogoliubov theory is applied to derive the ground state and excitation spectrum of the weakly interacting miscible BEC.
result: The analysis yields the ground state properties and collective excitations modified by altermagnetism.
conclusion: Altermagnetism introduces new features in the BEC, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper studies exceptional points in electromagnetic scattering of a sphere dimer, focusing on quasistatic and retarded regimes.
motivation: Exceptional points in scattering systems have applications in sensing and wave control, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze exceptional points of degeneracy in a sphere dimer using electromagnetic theory from quasistatic to fully retarded regimes.
result: They prove that PT-symmetric configurations exist in the quasistatic limit and study the transition to retarded regime.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for exceptional points in dimer scatterers but lacks relevance to the user's research interests.

method: Single crystals were grown using floating-zone method with high oxygen pressure treatment; properties were characterized by magnetic susceptibility, resistivity, and neutron diffraction.
result: Co doping suppresses the charge disproportionation and metal-insulator transition, leading to a ferromagnetic metallic state at low temperatures.
conclusion: Small Co doping significantly alters the electronic and magnetic ground state of CaFeO3, providing insight into the interplay between doping and charge ordering.

method: Experimental measurements of magnetization, specific heat, and neutron diffraction as functions of magnetic field and temperature.
result: A series of distinct magnetic phases including commensurate and incommensurate orders and magnetic soliton phases are observed.
conclusion: The phase diagram of CuB2O4 exhibits rich magnetic behavior that may be relevant for understanding frustrated magnetism.

motivation: To understand the role of Rashba spin-split states in driving nonlinear optical responses in topological insulators.
method: Steady-state and time-resolved second-harmonic generation measurements with polarization resolution on highly doped Bi1Te1.
result: Observation of magnetization-induced nonlinear optical response and signatures of Rashba spin-split states.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that Rashba spin-split states can be probed via second-harmonic generation, providing a new tool for investigating spin-textured states in topological materials.

title: Multiple Correlation Lengths And Type-1.5 Superconductivity In $u(1)$ Superconductors Due To Hidden Competition Between Irreducible Representations Of Nonlocal Pairing
authors: Anton Talkachov, Paul Leask, And Egor Babaev
abstract:

The ratio of magnetic field penetration length [MATH] and superconducting coherence length [MATH] is a defining quantity that governs magnetic response and underpins the conventional type-I and type-II classification of superconductors. While multicomponent superconductors are known to exhibit multiple co…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224520] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies type-1.5 superconductivity in U(1) superconductors with nonlocal pairing, revealing multiple correlation lengths due to hidden competition between irreducible representations.
motivation: To understand the magnetic response and classification of superconductors beyond the conventional type-I/type-II dichotomy, especially in multicomponent systems.
method: The authors analyze a U(1) superconductor model with nonlocal pairing interactions, deriving the Ginzburg-Landau free energy and computing the penetration depth and coherence lengths from the microscopic theory.
result: They find that hidden competition between different irreducible representations of the pairing interaction leads to multiple coherence lengths, resulting in type-1.5 superconductivity where vortices attract at long distances but repel at short distances.
conclusion: The work extends the classification of superconductors and provides a mechanism for type-1.5 behavior in single-component U(1) superconductors via nonlocal pairing.

motivation: To provide a more efficient method for constructing the Halperin state without requiring exact diagonalization of the parent Hamiltonian.
method: Derives a recursion relation for the second-quantized fermionic/bosonic Halperin state and validates it by proving the state satisfies the parent Hamiltonian.
result: The recursion relation is validated, offering a practical way to generate the Halperin state for larger systems.
conclusion: The second-quantized approach provides a scalable method to study Halperin states, relevant to fractional quantum Hall physics.

title: Skyrmion-resolved Topology In Chiral Topological Superconductors
authors: Bo-Wen Liu, Yu-Chen Zhuang, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Hao Wan, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:

Chiral topological superconductors (TSCs) are conventionally characterized by the bulk Chern number, which dictates the number of chiral Majorana modes at the boundary. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 235426] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals that the bulk Chern number in chiral topological superconductors can be decomposed into skyrmion numbers of the superconducting gap, providing a refined topological characterization.
motivation: The bulk Chern number alone obscures the rich momentum-space structure of the superconducting gap in chiral TSCs.
method: The authors analyze the momentum-space texture of the superconducting gap and decompose the Chern number into skyrmion numbers associated with gap nodes.
result: They show that the Chern number equals the sum of skyrmion numbers, and that skyrmion textures can be detected via spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy.
conclusion: Skyrmion-resolved topology offers a more detailed understanding of chiral TSCs and suggests experimental probes for the internal structure of the gap.

motivation: To explore how periodic driving and unconventional pairing can induce novel topological phases in superconducting systems.
method: The authors use Floquet theory and topological band theory to analyze the phase diagram and edge states of a ferromagnet-2DEG-superconductor heterostructure.
result: They identify anomalous Floquet higher-order topological superconducting phases characterized by Majorana corner modes.
conclusion: Periodic driving and unconventional pairing symmetries can stabilize higher-order topological superconductivity, offering new platforms for Majorana physics.

result: Observation of large isolated stripes and characterization of their properties.
conclusion: The study provides insights into stripe formation but is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Xiang Ji, Dengfeng Wang, Tong Zhou, And Xiaosen Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Ji, Dengfeng Wang, Tong Zhou, and Xiaosen Yang

We show that proximity to an altermagnet provides an efficient route to engineering non-Hermitian higher-order topological phases. The proximity-induced altermagnetic order gaps the edge states of a topological insulator, thereby driving a transition from a first-order to a second-order topological …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245420] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using altermagnets to engineer non-Hermitian higher-order topological insulators.
motivation: To find new ways to realize higher-order topological phases, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors theoretically show that proximity to an altermagnet can induce a transition from a first-order to a second-order topological insulator by gapping edge states.
result: They demonstrate that altermagnet engineering can create non-Hermitian higher-order topological phases.
conclusion: Altermagnets provide a viable route to engineer higher-order topological insulators, but the work is focused on topological phases without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Giant And Robust Josephson Diode Effect In Multiband Topological Nanowires
authors: Bao-Zong Wang, Zi-Kai Li, Zhong-Da Li, And Xiong-Jun Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Bao-Zong Wang, Zi-Kai Li, Zhong-Da Li, and Xiong-Jun Liu

We theoretically predict the giant and robust Josephson diode effect in quasi-one-dimensional topological Majorana nanowires in the regime with multiple subbands, which is expected to be relevant for the real experiment. In the multiband regime, the Majorana bound states and conventional Andreev bou…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220504] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts a giant and robust Josephson diode effect in multiband topological Majorana nanowires.
motivation: To explore the Josephson diode effect in a realistic multiband nanowire setup, which may be relevant for experiments.
method: Theoretical analysis of quasi-one-dimensional topological Majorana nanowires with multiple subbands, studying Majorana bound states and Andreev bound states.
result: A giant and robust Josephson diode effect is predicted in the multiband regime.
conclusion: Multiband topological nanowires can host a strong Josephson diode effect, which could be observed experimentally.

title: Triangular ${J}_{1}\text{−}{J}_{2}$ Heisenberg Antiferromagnet In A Magnetic Field
authors: T. Bader, S. Feng, S. Budaraju, F. Becca, J. Knolle, And F. Pollmann
abstract:
Author(s): T. Bader, S. Feng, S. Budaraju, F. Becca, J. Knolle, and F. Pollmann

The behavior of the paradigmatic [MATH] triangular lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet in a magnetic field remains unsettled despite decades of study. We map out the phase diagram using three complementary approaches, including self-consistent nonlinear spin-wave theory, density-mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241114] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of the triangular J1-J2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet in a magnetic field using spin-wave theory and DMRG.
motivation: The behavior of the triangular lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet in a magnetic field remains unresolved despite decades of study.
method: The authors use self-consistent nonlinear spin-wave theory, density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG), and exact diagonalization to map out the phase diagram.
result: They identify several magnetic phases and transitions as a function of magnetic field and frustration ratio.
conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive phase diagram for this paradigmatic model, clarifying long-standing questions.

title: Defect-mediated Melting Of Square-lattice Solids
abstract:
Author(s): William Grampel and Daniel Podolsky

The melting of two-dimensional solids is driven by the proliferation of topological defects, a mechanism described by Kosterlitz-Thouless-Halperin-Nelson-Young (KTHNY) theory for isotropic lattices. Here, the authors extend this theory to square-lattice solids, where lattice anisotropy introduces an additional elastic constant and modifies the interactions between defects. The theory predicts two-step melting through an intermediate tetratic phase, but with key differences from the isotropic case: a modified bound on the translational exponent and nonuniversal Young’s modulus at the solid–tetratic transition.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214109] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Extends KTHNY theory of two-dimensional melting to square-lattice solids, predicting a two-step melting process via an intermediate tetratic phase with modified elastic constants.
motivation: Understanding melting in anisotropic lattices is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper focuses on classical defect-mediated phase transitions without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors generalize KTHNY theory to square lattices by incorporating an additional elastic constant and analyzing defect interactions using renormalization group methods.
result: They find a modified bound on the translational exponent and nonuniversal Young's modulus at the solid–tetratic transition, differing from isotropic cases.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for melting in square-lattice solids, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spin-orbit Torques In Bulk Collinear Antiferromagnets: Complete Classification And Induced Spin Dynamics
authors: Yizhuo Song, Jianting Dong, Jiahao Shentu, Chen Wang, Yurong Su, And Jia Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yizhuo Song, Jianting Dong, Jiahao Shentu, Chen Wang, Yurong Su, and Jia Zhang

Current-induced spin-orbit torques (SOTs) provide a crucial mechanism for the electrical control of antiferromagnetic order. However, SOTs in antiferromagnets (AFMs) and the resulting spin dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here we present a complete classifications of SOTs in bulk collinear AFMs b…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224432] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper classifies spin-orbit torques in bulk collinear antiferromagnets and studies the induced spin dynamics.
motivation: Spin-orbit torques provide a mechanism for electrical control of antiferromagnetic order, which is important for spintronics but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors present a complete classification of spin-orbit torques in bulk collinear antiferromagnets using symmetry analysis and model the resulting spin dynamics.
result: They identify all possible torque components and show how they drive antiferromagnetic dynamics.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of current-induced control in antiferromagnets but does not connect to the user's research interests.

title: Bi-isotropic Effects On Hybrid Surface Polaritons In Bilayer Configurations
authors: Ariel Nonato And Pedro D. S. Silva
abstract:
Author(s): Ariel Nonato and Pedro D. S. Silva

In this work, we investigate the bi-isotropic effects in the formation and tunability of hybrid surface polaritons in bilayer configurations. To do that, we consider a heterostructure constituted with layers formed by a TI medium endowed with bi-isotropic constitutive relations and an AFM medium. Us…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224434] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bi-isotropic effects on hybrid surface polaritons in a bilayer of topological insulator and antiferromagnet, focusing on electromagnetic wave propagation.
motivation: To understand how bi-isotropic constitutive relations affect the formation and tunability of hybrid surface polaritons in layered structures.
method: Theoretical analysis using Maxwell's equations with bi-isotropic and antiferromagnetic media, solving for dispersion relations of surface polaritons.
result: Bi-isotropy introduces new tunability and hybridization effects in surface polariton modes.
conclusion: Bi-isotropic materials can be used to control surface polaritons in bilayer configurations, with potential applications in photonics.

title: Gap Reopening As A Possible Signature Of Coupling Between Majorana Zero Modes In $\mathrm{Sn}\text{−}{(\mathrm{Bi},\mathrm{Sb})}_{2}{(\mathrm{Te},\mathrm{S})}_{3}$-based Josephson Trijunctions
authors: Duolin Wang, Xiang Zhang, Yunxiao Zhang, Heng Zhang, Fucong Fei, Xiang Wang, Bing Li, Xiaozhou Yang, Yukun Shi, Zhongmou Jia, Enna Zhuo, Yuyang Huang, Anqi Wang, Zenan Shi, Zhaozheng Lyu, Xiaohui Song, Peiling Li, Bingbing Tong, Ziwei Dou, Jie Shen, Guangtong Liu, Fanming Qu, Fengqi Song, And Li Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Duolin Wang, Xiang Zhang, Yunxiao Zhang, Heng Zhang, Fucong Fei, Xiang Wang, Bing Li, Xiaozhou Yang, Yukun Shi, Zhongmou Jia, Enna Zhuo, Yuyang Huang, Anqi Wang, Zenan Shi, Zhaozheng Lyu, Xiaohui Song, Peiling Li, Bingbing Tong, Ziwei Dou, Jie Shen, Guangtong Liu, Fanming Qu, Fengqi Song, and Li Lu

Here, the authors report the experimental observation of a possible signature of coupling between Majorana zero modes in two adjacent Josephson trijunctions fabricated on the surface of the topological insulator Sn-(Bi,Sb)
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235424] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of gap reopening in Sn-(Bi,Sb)2(Te,S)3-based Josephson trijunctions as a possible signature of coupling between Majorana zero modes.
motivation: To detect coupling between Majorana zero modes in a topological insulator-based Josephson trijunction, which is crucial for validating the Fu-Kane theory and advancing topological quantum computation.
method: Fabrication of two adjacent Josephson trijunctions on the surface of the topological insulator Sn-(Bi,Sb)2(Te,S)3 and measurement of the minigap via transport spectroscopy.
result: Observation of minigap reopening at both trijunction centers, whereas individual trijunctions would show gap closure, indicating coupling between Majorana zero modes.
conclusion: The results provide experimental support for the Fu-Kane theory and motivate further development of topological quantum computation schemes based on Majorana zero modes.

title: Exceptional Horns In $n$-root Graphene And Lieb Photonic Ring Lattices
authors: A. M. Marques, D. Viedma, V. Ahufinger, And R. G. Dias

A realistic photonic ring design using tailored gain and loss demonstrates how these models can be realized experimentally.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245136] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies exceptional points and flat bands in n-root graphene and Lieb photonic lattices, focusing on non-Hermitian topology and photonic realizations.
motivation: To explore the effects of non-Hermiticity and higher-root topology in lattice models, and to propose experimental realizations in photonic ring lattices.
method: The authors construct n-root versions of graphene and Lieb lattices using unidirectional coupling loops, analyze their band structures, and design a photonic ring lattice with gain and loss.
result: Dirac points become exceptional horns with sublinear scaling, Landau levels show fractional flux dependence, and extra zero-energy flat bands appear from sublattice imbalance.
conclusion: These models reveal novel exceptional topology and can be realized experimentally in photonic systems.

title: Valence Band Satellite, And Temperature-dependent Magnetic And Spectral Study Of $α\text{−}\mathrm{Fe}$
authors: Trishu Verma, Shivani Bhardwaj, And Sudhir K. Pandey
abstract:
Author(s): Trishu Verma, Shivani Bhardwaj, and Sudhir K. Pandey

We investigate the influence of correlations and plasmonic excitation on the valence band satellite of [MATH]-Fe, along with magnetic and spectral properties as a function of temperature. Coulomb interaction parameters are obtained by systematically employing various schemes within the constrained rand…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the valence band satellite and temperature-dependent magnetic and spectral properties of α-Fe using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the influence of correlations and plasmonic excitations on the electronic structure and magnetism of iron.
method: Density functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) and constrained random phase approximation.
result: Coulomb interaction parameters are extracted, and the temperature dependence of magnetic moments and spectral functions is computed.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the correlated electronic structure of α-Fe, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Spin Liquid Ground State With The Evidence Of Roton-like Excitations At Elevated Temperatures In The Triangular-lattice Delafossite ${\mathrm{YbCuSe}}_{2}$
authors: K. Bhattacharya, Y. Tokiwa, And M. Majumder
abstract:
Author(s): K. Bhattacharya, Y. Tokiwa, and M. Majumder

Theory predicts that frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets host roton-like excitations (RLEs) between two characteristic temperature scales. While signatures of RLEs have been observed in a few systems with magnetically ordered ground states, they have been unobserved in a system that has a quantum spin liquid (QSL) ground state. Here, using heat capacity and muon spin relaxation measurements on single-crystalline YbCuSe
[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220407] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports evidence of roton-like excitations in a triangular-lattice quantum spin liquid candidate YbCuSe2.
motivation: Roton-like excitations have been predicted in frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets but not observed in systems with a quantum spin liquid ground state; this work aims to fill that gap.
method: Heat capacity and muon spin relaxation measurements on single-crystalline YbCuSe2.
result: The authors demonstrate the presence of roton-like excitations at elevated temperatures prior to the quantum spin liquid ground state.
conclusion: The observation of roton-like excitations in a quantum spin liquid system provides new insights into the physics of frustrated magnets.

title: Interplay Between Many-body Correlations, Strain, And Lattice Relaxation In Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Lorenzo Crippa, Gautam Rai, Dumitru Călugăru, Haoyu Hu, Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, B. Andrei Bernevig, Roser Valentí, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Tim Wehling
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Crippa, Gautam Rai, Dumitru Călugăru, Haoyu Hu, Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, B. Andrei Bernevig, Roser Valentí, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Tim Wehling

Here, the authors explain a set of experimental features that, while ubiquitously observed in twisted bilayer graphene samples, have so far eluded a unified theoretical description. A broad range of spectral, response, and thermodynamic properties in twisted bilayer graphene is accurately described microscopically and traced to the interplay of electronic correlations, lattice strain, and structural relaxation. The results are in excellent agreement with multiple recent experiments including scanning tunneling and quantum twisting microscopy experiments.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241112] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains experimental features in twisted bilayer graphene by modeling the interplay of electronic correlations, strain, and lattice relaxation.
motivation: Many experimental features in twisted bilayer graphene lack a unified theoretical description.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model incorporating electronic correlations, lattice strain, and structural relaxation, and compare with experimental data.
result: The model accurately describes a broad range of spectral, response, and thermodynamic properties observed in experiments.
conclusion: The interplay of correlations, strain, and relaxation is key to understanding twisted bilayer graphene's properties.

title: Altermagnetism Of Ultrathin CrSb Slabs
authors: Brahim Marfoua, Mohammad Amirabbasi, And Marcus Ekholm
abstract:
Author(s): Brahim Marfoua, Mohammad Amirabbasi, and Marcus Ekholm

Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, combining characteristics of both ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, making them highly interesting for spintronics applications. CrSb is a prime candidate with a high Néel temperature ($∼700{0ex}…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214439] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the altermagnetic properties of ultrathin CrSb slabs using first-principles calculations.
motivation: Altermagnets are promising for spintronics due to momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, and CrSb has a high Néel temperature, making it a candidate for thin-film applications.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations are performed to investigate the electronic structure and magnetic properties of CrSb slabs of varying thickness.
result: The authors find that altermagnetism persists in ultrathin slabs, with thickness-dependent modifications to the spin splitting and magnetic anisotropy.
conclusion: Ultrathin CrSb slabs retain altermagnetic order, suggesting potential for spintronic devices at reduced dimensions.

title: Ferrimagnetic Blume-Emery-Griffiths Sawtooth Chain: Spin Ice And Quasiordering
authors: A. A. Zvyagin And G. A. Zvyagina
abstract:
Author(s): A. A. Zvyagin and G. A. Zvyagina

The ferrimagnetic Blume-Emery-Griffiths one-dimensional model on the sawtooth chain with bilinear and biquadratic interactions between spins is studied exactly. Conditions at which the characteristic feature of spin ices, the remnant entropy at zero magnetic field appears, are studied. On the other …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an exactly solvable ferrimagnetic Blume-Emery-Griffiths model on a sawtooth chain, focusing on spin ice behavior and remnant entropy.
motivation: To understand the conditions for spin ice features and quasiordering in a one-dimensional frustrated magnetic system.
method: Exact solution of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model on a sawtooth chain using transfer matrix or Bethe ansatz techniques.
result: Identifies parameter regimes where remnant entropy (characteristic of spin ice) appears and describes quasiordering phenomena.
conclusion: The model exhibits spin-ice-like residual entropy and quasi-long-range order, providing insights into frustrated magnetism in low dimensions.

title: Bilateral Hydrogenation-induced high-Chern-number Quantum Anomalous Hall State In Monolayer ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{6}$
authors: Xiang Li, Xin-Wei Yi, Jing-Yang You, Jia-Wen Li, Qing-Han Yang, Gang Su, And Bo Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Xin-Wei Yi, Jing-Yang You, Jia-Wen Li, Qing-Han Yang, Gang Su, and Bo Gu

The pursuit of high-temperature quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) insulators faces fundamental challenges, including narrow topological gaps and low Curie temperatures ([MATH]) in existing materials. Here, we propose a transformative strategy using bilateral hydrogenation to engineer a robust Q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224430] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes bilateral hydrogenation to engineer a high-Chern-number quantum anomalous Hall state in monolayer Cr2Ge2Te6, focusing on topological properties and Curie temperature enhancement.
motivation: The pursuit of high-temperature quantum anomalous Hall insulators is hindered by narrow topological gaps and low Curie temperatures in existing materials.
method: First-principles calculations are used to study the electronic structure and topological properties of hydrogenated monolayer Cr2Ge2Te6.
result: Bilateral hydrogenation induces a high-Chern-number QAH state with an enhanced topological gap and increased Curie temperature.
conclusion: Bilateral hydrogenation is an effective strategy to realize robust QAH states in two-dimensional materials.

title: Effect Of Spin-orbit Coupling On Spin And Orbital Ordering In ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{n+1}{\mathrm{Cr}}_{n}{\mathrm{O}}_{3n+1}$ ($n=1$, 2)
authors: Cristian Fanjul And A. A. Aligia

We incorporate spin-orbit coupling (SOC) into effective Kugel-Khomskii models for the [MATH] and [MATH] members of the Ruddlesden-Popper series [MATH]. These models contain interacting spins 1 and pseudospins 1/2 at each site describing spin and orbit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235130] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-orbit coupling effects on spin and orbital ordering in Sr-based Ruddlesden-Popper compounds using effective Kugel-Khomskii models.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling with spin and orbital degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems.
method: Effective Kugel-Khomskii models incorporating spin-orbit coupling are derived and analyzed for the n=1 and n=2 members of the Sr_{n+1}Cr_nO_{3n+1} series.
result: The models predict specific spin and orbital ordering patterns influenced by spin-orbit coupling.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling significantly modifies the magnetic and orbital order, which may be relevant for understanding the physics of these materials.

title: Persistent Current And Orbital Magnetization Along A Valley-contrasting Junction In Bilayer Graphene In A Magnetic Field
abstract:
Author(s): K. Shizuya

In a magnetic field, bilayer graphene hosts an octet of pseudo-zero-mode (PZM) electron levels nearly degenerate in orbitals [MATH], valleys, and spins. They split in valleys by electrostatic gating. In gated bilayer graphene, in which the interlayer bias is set up to flip sign across a line, one…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235422] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies persistent current and orbital magnetization in a valley-contrasting junction in bilayer graphene under a magnetic field.
motivation: To understand the electronic properties of gated bilayer graphene with a sign-flipping interlayer bias, which creates a valley-contrasting junction.
method: Theoretical analysis using a low-energy continuum model for bilayer graphene in a magnetic field, solving for pseudo-zero-mode levels and computing persistent currents and orbital magnetization.
result: The valley-contrasting junction leads to persistent currents and orbital magnetization that depend on the junction geometry and magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings reveal new magneto-electronic phenomena in bilayer graphene junctions, relevant for valleytronics and quantum transport.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation in structured populations despite the payoff advantage of defection.
method: Game-theoretic model on a lattice where interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum of players' wealth, analyzed via statistical physics methods.
result: A discontinuous wealth-gradient transition drives cooperation, revealing a hidden pathway to cooperation.
conclusion: Wealth gradients can promote cooperation in structured populations, offering insights into social dynamics.

title: ChronoCast: A Time-series Paradigm For Molecular Dynamics Simulation Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
authors: Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, And Jie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, and Jie Chen

We propose a time-series paradigm named ChronoCast for molecular dynamics simulation using an advanced autoregressive Equivariant Graph Neural Network, which reformulates the conventionally time-consuming integration process into a forecasting task. This reformulation in turn offers a promising solu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065305] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: ChronoCast uses an equivariant graph neural network to forecast molecular dynamics trajectories, replacing traditional numerical integration.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to small time steps; a time-series forecasting approach can accelerate simulations.
method: An autoregressive equivariant graph neural network is trained on MD trajectory data to predict future atomic positions and velocities.
result: The method achieves accurate long-term predictions with significant speedup compared to traditional integration.
conclusion: Machine learning can effectively surrogate MD integration, enabling faster simulations while preserving physical accuracy.

title: Universality And Ambiguity In Extremes Of Anomalous Diffusion
abstract:
Author(s): Sean D. Lawley

Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffus…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of fastest first-passage times in anomalous diffusion processes, focusing on subdiffusion and superdiffusion.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many; understanding extreme first-passage times is crucial for modeling such phenomena.
method: The author derives asymptotic formulas for the fastest first-passage time in anomalous diffusion models, analyzing the dependence on the number of searchers and the anomalous exponent.
result: The fastest first-passage time vanishes logarithmically for subdiffusion and can be faster than for normal diffusion, with universal scaling laws but also ambiguity due to model details.
conclusion: The results highlight universal features and ambiguities in extreme statistics of anomalous diffusion, relevant to biophysical search processes.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijit Bera and Kevin E. Bassler

Variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) are a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes that unify a broad range of previously studied models within a single parametrized framework. Their dynamics consist of discrete random steps, or flights, during which the walker's speed varies…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, a class of stochastic processes.
motivation: To unify and understand a broad range of anomalous diffusion models within a single parametrized framework.
method: The authors analyze variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) using mathematical decomposition techniques to characterize the diffusion behavior.
result: They achieve a complete decomposition of the anomalous diffusion, revealing the underlying mechanisms and scaling properties.
conclusion: The work provides a unified theoretical framework for anomalous diffusion, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics.
motivation: To understand the statistical properties of single-particle trajectories in complex environments.
method: Reformulates the time-averaged displacement correlation function in terms of velocity correlation functions within the generalized Langevin equation framework.
result: Identifies scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
conclusion: The derived scaling laws provide insight into the dynamics of single-particle tracking.

title: Yielding In Dense Active Matter
authors: Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, And M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, and M. Lisa Manning

High-density granular active matter is a useful model for dense animal collectives and could be useful for designing reconfigurable materials that can flow or solidify on command. Recent work has demonstrated key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065410] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies yielding behavior in dense granular active matter as a model for animal collectives and reconfigurable materials.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical response of dense active matter is important for designing materials that can flow or solidify on command and for modeling animal collectives.
method: The authors use numerical simulations or theoretical modeling to analyze the yielding transition in high-density granular active matter.
result: Key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and passive systems are identified.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the yielding behavior of active matter, which may inform the design of reconfigurable materials.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
