We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, which is relevant for understanding axion-insulating phases.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface magnetic order.
conclusion: The surface ferromagnon mode is a signature of the axion-insulating phase, providing insight into the interplay between magnetism and topology.

title: Confinement And Finite-range Effects In A Quasi-two-dimensional Gas Of Fermionic Dimers
authors: Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, And Grigory E. Astrakharchik
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, and Grigory E. Astrakharchik

A study of a gas of fermionic dimers in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry induced by strong harmonic confinement in one direction is presented. Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo calculations are used to quantify the effects of confinement and finite interaction range on the equation of state and density profiles, with the results benchmarked against analytical theories.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022051] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo study of fermionic dimers in a quasi-2D geometry, focusing on confinement and finite-range effects on the equation of state.
motivation: To understand how strong confinement and finite interaction range affect the properties of a gas of fermionic dimers, relevant to ultracold atomic systems.
method: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the equation of state and density profiles, benchmarked against analytical theories.
result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range, providing benchmarks for analytical models.
conclusion: The study provides insights into quasi-2D fermionic dimer gases, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence using the Onsager-Machlup formulation, focusing on most probable paths and invariant sets.
motivation: Understanding turbulence transition from bistable states triggered by noise is a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics.
method: The authors apply the Onsager-Machlup functional to compute most probable transition paths and analyze invariant sets in a stochastic dynamical system.
result: They identify key invariant sets and characterize the most probable paths for noise-induced transitions to turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the role of noise in triggering turbulence, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: To develop a systematic method for reconstructing probability distributions from experimental data, which is an inverse problem.
method: Applies information geometry to define a manifold structure on the space of probability distributions and uses geodesic transformations to map between distributions.
result: Demonstrates the method on synthetic and experimental data, showing improved reconstruction accuracy compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Information geometry provides a principled framework for transforming probability distributions, useful for inverse problems in data analysis.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting and explaining dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies time-modulated resonant photonic circuits that achieve complete inelastic transparency, converting input light frequency and potentially amplifying power.
motivation: To understand and exploit time modulation in photonic circuits for frequency conversion and power amplification.
method: Theoretical analysis of resonant photonic circuits with time-varying parameters, using coupled-mode theory and scattering matrix formalism.
result: Complete inelastic transparency is demonstrated, where input light is fully converted to output at shifted frequencies without reflection.
conclusion: Time-modulated photonic circuits can achieve perfect frequency conversion and amplification, with potential applications in optical communication and signal processing.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework for constructing classical spin Hamiltonians from noncollinear spin DFT using spin-cluster expansion fitted to magnetic torques.
motivation: To enable accurate and efficient modeling of complex magnetic systems beyond simple Heisenberg models.
method: Combines noncollinear spin DFT with spin-cluster expansion, fitting the model to magnetic torques instead of total energies.
result: Demonstrates that the torque-based fitting yields accurate spin Hamiltonians with fewer DFT calculations.
conclusion: The proposed framework is a practical tool for studying magnetic materials with complex spin textures.

title: Visualizing Phonon Edge States On Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, And Jakob Schiøtz
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, and Jakob Schiøtz

Enhanced atomic vibrations have previously been observed near edges of two-dimensional materials with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM). Here this observation is accounted for by localized phonon edge modes by including correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022049] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM were not well understood; the authors aimed to explain this phenomenon.
method: They included correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations to model the effect of localized phonon edge modes.
result: The simulations reproduced the enhanced vibrations, confirming that they arise from phonon edge modes.
conclusion: Phonon edge modes are responsible for the observed enhanced atomic vibrations at edges of MoS2.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative modulation and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, analyzed for convergence and self-attention emergence.
motivation: To bridge neuroscience-inspired associative memory with self-attention mechanisms in machine learning, using astrocyte modulation as a biological plausible gain control.
method: Formulates coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics with a Lyapunov function and entropy-regularized replicator equation, then analyzes fixed points and emergent attention patterns.
result: The model converges globally and at fixed points exhibits self-attention-like behavior, with astrocytic gains shaping effective connectivity.
conclusion: Astrocyte-gated dynamics can naturally give rise to self-attention, suggesting a biological basis for attention mechanisms and a new class of associative memory models.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network approach that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems with millions of atoms, demonstrated on twisted trilayer graphene and other moiré systems.
conclusion: The tensor network methodology provides a scalable tool for studying electronic properties of complex moiré systems.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and become detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to condensed matter physics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is applied to chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be detected via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of chiral soliton dynamics, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to regularize three-dimensional fermionic CFTs and perform numerical simulations to compute spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and accurately compute scaling dimensions and operator content.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs and can reveal emergent symmetries like supersymmetry.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superlattices, which are of interest for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2.
result: They identify three distinct, tunable magnetic phases and demonstrate a general framework for designing spin moiré superstructures.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for engineering spin textures in moiré materials, with potential applications in information storage and processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps near the Curie point for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial but challenging; the authors aim to leverage physical principles to improve link prediction.
method: The framework integrates domain knowledge from physics (e.g., conservation laws, symmetries) with network data to infer causal links.
result: The method demonstrates improved accuracy in predicting physical links across various networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can enhance causal inference in networks, offering a principled way to incorporate domain knowledge.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers, a topological condensed matter phenomenon.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers driven by topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches.
result: Anyonic exciton superfluidity emerges near topological criticality, offering a robust mechanism for engineering such states.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for realizing anyonic superfluids, advancing the study of topological phases.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a hidden order with time-reversal symmetry breaking.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and theoretical modeling.
result: The transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class, and the ground state breaks time-reversal symmetry, as evidenced by nonlinear susceptibility.
conclusion: The study establishes HoAgGe as a rare example of a kagome ice compound with a hidden order and provides insights into frustrated magnetism.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesized layered transition-metal oxyhalides and performed angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure.
result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising system for exploring flat-band physics and potentially correlated phases at accessible temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy is employed as a probe to detect the quantum anomalous Hall state and its magnetic ordering under applied electric fields.
result: The experiments reveal a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and show that an electric field can switch between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism, relevant for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, focusing on density fluctuations and critical opalescence suppression.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and how this affects the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to examine the critical properties of a model of spinning particles that form a hyperuniform fluid.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusually calm behavior (suppressed fluctuations) yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, with implications for understanding phase transitions in systems with constrained fluctuations.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin-dependent electron optics in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling spin valve functionality.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene heterostructures, with gate-tunable ballistic transport.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: Ballistic spin valves in graphene can be realized using electron optics, offering a new mechanism for spintronic devices.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines robotic metamaterial experiments with theoretical modeling to probe the percolation of active forces.
result: Finds that when active units are too sparse, increasing activity reduces the macroscopic active response.
conclusion: Activity does not always enhance response; percolation of active forces is crucial for macroscopic effects.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for topological data analysis with exponential speedup, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; the paper aims to demonstrate quantum advantage in this domain.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that computes persistence diagrams using quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques.
result: They prove an exponential speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of topological data analysis.
conclusion: The work highlights potential quantum advantage in data analysis but is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap bridging the gap between theoretical quantum computing and practical applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of current quantum computing progress.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but does not present new technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to provide an end-to-end implementation on current quantum hardware.
method: The paper describes a complete quantum algorithm pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, implemented on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the approximation of the Jones polynomial for various knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and highlighting resource requirements.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and provides insights into the potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific states or require many resources.
method: The authors propose a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition that decomposes any target photonic state into a sequence of photon catalysis operations, which are experimentally feasible with current technology.
result: They show that any multimode multi-photon state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: This work provides a general and scalable framework for photonic state preparation, potentially enabling new quantum information protocols.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged established theories.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and magneto-optical phenomena.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving with expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and potential applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome lattice materials, analyzing electronic structure and many-body effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for studying correlated electron physics and may lead to new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.

result: The paper tracks progress in the field and highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain an active area with future research opportunities, but the paper is not aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic phases of matter with potential applications in quantum computing, but this review does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, discussing chiral edge modes and topological order.
result: Summarizes progress in identifying Kitaev spin liquid candidates and their properties.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of condensed matter physics, but the paper does not contribute to the user's specific research directions.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for modeling neural networks, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open challenges in accurately modeling internal conversion in complex systems.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to better understand and control internal conversion for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.

tldr: A colloquium review of quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including interactions underlying their formation and quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, covering topological field configurations, spin patterns, and quantum effects.
result: Summarizes current understanding of skyrmion quantum properties and their potential for spintronic applications.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may enable novel functionalities, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker

result: Summarizes current constraints and future prospects for various spin-dependent interaction searches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential to reveal new physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To explore how massive quantum systems can serve as interfaces to study gravity, addressing the least precisely tested natural force.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current state-of-the-art and outlines future directions for testing quantum gravity with massive quantum systems.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to probe gravity at the quantum level, but significant experimental challenges remain.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: Presents PyOpticL, an open-source Python library for modular optical layout, demonstrated with a laser system for trapped-ion qubit operations achieving >99% gate fidelity.
motivation: Complex optical systems in quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions are not scalable due to conventional piecewise setup; a modular, code-to-CAD approach is needed.
method: Developed PyOpticL, a Python library using beam-path simulation and dynamic routing to place optical elements without a priori specification, enabling modular 'drop-in' baseplates for common subsystems.
result: Demonstrated a full laser system for strontium trapped ions, achieving laser cooling, qubit state detection, and single-qubit gates with over 99% fidelity using 3D-printed baseplates.
conclusion: The modular optical design paradigm enables scaling of optical systems for quantum computers and fosters open-source collaborative hardware design.

title: Experimental Exclusion Of A Generalized Károlyházy Gravity-induced Decoherence Model
authors: Nicola Bortolotti, Kristian Piscicchia, Alessio Porcelli, Matthias Laubenstein, Simone Manti, Antonino Marcianò, Federico Nola And Catalina Curceanu
abstract: We report new experimental constraints on the generalized version of the gravity-induced decoherence model originally proposed by Károlyházy. Using data collected by the VIP Collaboration at the INFN Gran Sasso National Laboratory with a high-purity germanium detector, we derive an improved lower bound on the spatial correlation length characterizing metric fluctuations in the model. We obtain a bound m (95% C.L.), which exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the previous experimental limit. When combined with the theoretical upper bound m derived from macroscopic localization requirements, our result excludes the generalized Károlyházy model. The same conclusion applies to an associated non-Markovian formulation of the continuous spontaneous localization model. Our findings significantly tighten experimental constraints on gravity-related decoherence scenarios and demonstrate the sensitivity of underground low-background experiments to foundational modifications of quantum mechanics.
tldr: Experimental constraints exclude a gravity-induced decoherence model using underground detector data.
motivation: To test whether gravity causes wavefunction collapse, which is a foundational question in quantum mechanics.
method: Analyzed data from the VIP Collaboration's high-purity germanium detector at Gran Sasso to bound the spatial correlation length of metric fluctuations.
result: Obtained a lower bound on the correlation length exceeding the previous limit by an order of magnitude, excluding the generalized Károlyházy model.
conclusion: The model is ruled out, tightening constraints on gravity-related decoherence and spontaneous localization models.

title: A Maxwell Fish-eye Lens In A Bose–Einstein Condensate
authors: Jelte Duchêne, Elinor Kath, Floriane Arrouas, Hanyi Jang, Helmut Strobel, Markus K Oberthaler, Jay Mehta, Liam M Farrell, Wyatt Kirkby And Duncan H J O’dell
abstract: We experimentally realize an analogue of the optical Maxwell fish-eye lens (MFEL) using phononic excitations in a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC). A MFEL is characterized by a radially symmetric, spatially varying refractive index with the remarkable property that rays emitted from any point within the lens are perfectly focused at their antipodal points. While the implementation of such gradient-index lenses is challenging in conventional optical systems, BECs offer a highly tunable platform in which the spatially varying speed of sound of collective excitations—phonons, the acoustic analogues of photons—can be engineered and their dynamics observed in real time. Time-resolved measurements of phonon wavefronts reveal focusing behavior that shows good agreement with analytical theory and numerical simulations. This work provides both a geometric and physical framework for engineering effective refractive indices using ultracold atoms, and simulating wave propagation on effective spherical geometries.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes an analogue of the Maxwell fish-eye lens using phononic excitations in a Bose-Einstein condensate, demonstrating focusing of sound waves.
motivation: To explore analogies between optical systems and Bose-Einstein condensates, and to demonstrate a highly tunable platform for simulating wave propagation on curved geometries.
method: The authors engineer a spatially varying speed of sound in a BEC to create a gradient-index lens for phonons, and measure phonon wavefronts in real time.
result: Time-resolved measurements show focusing behavior consistent with analytical theory and numerical simulations.
conclusion: BECs provide a versatile platform for simulating wave propagation in effective curved spaces and for realizing gradient-index lenses.

title: Anisotropic Fluorescence Signals Retarded Dipole-dipole Interactions In A Thermal Atomic Cloud
authors: Vyacheslav Shatokhin, Friedemann Landmesser, Mario Niebuhr, Frank Stienkemeier, Andreas Buchleitner And Lukas Bruder
abstract: We experimentally observe and theoretically explain anisotropic multiple quantum coherence signals in the fluorescence from dilute thermal potassium vapours, at room temperature and particle densities . We identify the retarded part of the geometrically fully resolved inter-atomic, resonant dipole-dipole interaction as the crucial ingredient to theoretically reproduce all qualitative features of the experimental spectra.
tldr: Experimental and theoretical study of anisotropic fluorescence signals from thermal atomic vapors due to retarded dipole-dipole interactions.
motivation: To understand the role of retarded dipole-dipole interactions in anisotropic multiple quantum coherence signals observed in fluorescence from thermal atomic clouds.
method: Experimental observation of fluorescence from dilute thermal potassium vapors combined with theoretical modeling incorporating geometrically resolved retarded dipole-dipole interactions.
result: The retarded part of the dipole-dipole interaction is essential to reproduce all qualitative features of the experimental spectra.
conclusion: Retarded dipole-dipole interactions significantly influence anisotropic fluorescence signals in thermal atomic clouds, providing insight into inter-atomic interactions at room temperature.

title: Percolation With Coupled Lasers: Effect Of Non-linearities On The Phase Transition
authors: Simon Mahler, Nikita Stroev, Mahmoud Abu Rmilah, Asher Friesem And Nir Davidson
abstract: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are challenging due to difficulties in tuning site connectivity, isolating local interactions, and mitigating finite-size effects. In this work, we experimentally investigate percolation with a platform of coupled lasers, where connectivity, interaction strength, and system size can be controlled. Using a square array of lasers with astronomical number of possible cluster configurations, we show that the emergence of a percolating cluster corresponds to the onset of phase locking among the lasers. We also show that the percolation probability undergoes a second-order alike transition as a function of the site-occupation probability, with a threshold consistent with classical theoretical predictions. Surprisingly, we find that at low pump level, amplified mode competition (nonlinear regime) alters the effective behavior of the lasing sites and modify the nature of the percolation transition. The experimental results are interpreted by the means of a theoretical toy model with connectivity rules to the classical percolation.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies percolation using a coupled laser array, showing that the percolation transition corresponds to phase locking and that nonlinearities modify the transition.
motivation: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are challenging; coupled lasers offer a tunable platform to investigate percolation dynamics.
method: A square array of coupled lasers with controllable connectivity and pump levels is used to observe percolation and phase locking, with a toy model to interpret results.
result: Percolation probability undergoes a second-order-like transition consistent with classical theory, but nonlinearities at low pump alter the transition nature.
conclusion: Coupled lasers provide a versatile platform for percolation studies, revealing nonlinear effects on phase transitions.

title: Nonreciprocal Electrical Transport In Emerging Noncentrosymmetric Systems: From Hidden Symmetry To Functional Devices
authors: Shengyao Li, Zherui Yang, Xueyan Wang, Kian Ping Loh And X Renshaw Wang
abstract: Contrary to the reciprocal electrical transport constrained by the Onsager relations, nonreciprocal electrical transport arises in noncentrosymmetric systems where the resistance depends on the direction of current flow or external stimuli such as a magnetic field. Governed by symmetry-dependent charge dynamics, these responses appear as nonreciprocal charge transport (NCT) in the longitudinal direction and the nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) in the transverse direction. Recent theoretical advances have expanded the range of mechanisms and material platforms capable of hosting nonreciprocal signals, revealing the role of hidden band-geometric properties. In parallel, experimental developments have exploited these effects for practical devices, offering promising alternatives to semiconductor-based rectifiers and wireless components, with advantages in broadband operation, ultrafast response, and high energy efficiency. In this review, we summarize electrical measurement techniques and characteristic transport signatures for identifying nonreciprocal phenomena and uncovering their underlying symmetry. We provide a comprehensive discussion of the fundamental mechanisms underlying NCT and NLHE, organized through representative material systems, and a subsequent examination of strategies for artificially inducing and enhancing nonreciprocity. Finally, we evaluate the technological perspectives of nonreciprocal electrical transport for electronic applications, along with key challenges and opportunities for scalable device implementation. By synthesizing current progress, this review aims to guide materials discovery and device innovation, and to inspire exploration of new symmetry settings and unconventional routes toward enhanced nonreciprocal functionalities.
tldr: A review of nonreciprocal electrical transport in noncentrosymmetric systems, focusing on symmetry-dependent charge dynamics and device applications.
motivation: To understand and harness nonreciprocal transport phenomena for electronic devices beyond conventional semiconductors.
method: Summarizes theoretical mechanisms (band-geometric properties) and experimental techniques for measuring nonreciprocal charge transport and nonlinear Hall effect.
result: Identifies hidden symmetries and material platforms that enable nonreciprocal responses, and demonstrates potential for broadband, ultrafast rectifiers.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal transport offers a promising route for next-generation electronic devices, but challenges remain in material scalability and integration.

title: Duality Between Correlation Functions And Wilson Loops In Gauge Theory From Effective Field Theory
authors: Hao Chen, Pier Francesco Monni, Zhaoyan Pang, Gherardo Vita, And Hua Xing Zhu

tldr: This paper studies correlation functions and Wilson loops in gauge theories using effective field theory, focusing on QCD in the sequential light-cone limit.
motivation: To understand the structure of multi-point correlation functions in gauge theories and their relation to Wilson loops, which is important for high-energy physics and QCD.
method: The authors use soft-collinear effective field theory (SCET) to derive a factorization theorem for the four-point correlation function of vector currents in the sequential light-cone limit.
result: They establish a duality between correlation functions and Wilson loops in this limit, providing a systematic framework for computing such observables.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of gauge theory correlation functions and may have implications for precision QCD calculations.

In this work, we develop a kinetic theory of stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) based on a generalized Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) model incorporating a velocity-dependent collision frequency. Starting from the Boltzmann equation, we derive an analytic expression for the SBS gain coefficient that…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063523] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a kinetic theory of stimulated Brillouin scattering using a velocity-dependent collision model.
motivation: To improve the theoretical description of SBS in plasmas by incorporating more realistic collision physics.
method: Derives an analytic SBS gain coefficient from the Boltzmann equation with a generalized BGK collision term.
result: Obtains an expression for the SBS gain that accounts for velocity-dependent collisional relaxation.
conclusion: The velocity-dependent model provides a more accurate description of SBS, relevant to laser-plasma interactions.

motivation: To characterize Rydberg states in dysprosium, which is important for applications in quantum simulation and sensing, but the paper focuses on atomic physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Two-color trap depletion spectroscopy in a magneto-optical trap combined with multichannel quantum defect theory analysis.
result: Measured and assigned over 700 Rydberg states, identified six perturbing states belonging to higher ionization limits.
conclusion: The work provides a benchmark for dysprosium Rydberg states, aiding future experiments with Rydberg atoms.

tldr: This paper uses multiplet ligand-field theory with Wannier orbitals to compute X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) spectra for the altermagnet α-Fe2O3.
motivation: Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials with potential spintronic applications; understanding their XMCD spectra aids experimental characterization.
method: The authors employ multiplet ligand-field theory combined with Wannier orbitals to simulate XMCD spectra, accounting for crystal field and spin-orbit coupling.
result: They reproduce experimental XMCD features and explain the spectral differences between the easy-axis and easy-plane phases of hematite.
conclusion: The theoretical approach provides a reliable framework for interpreting XMCD of altermagnets, but the work is primarily a materials characterization study.

result: Observation of a cluster-liquid-like state and enhanced magnetocaloric effect in these frustrated spin-hexamer lattices.
conclusion: These materials provide a new platform for studying frustration and magnetocaloric effects, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Bond-rigidity Heterogeneity Induced Anomalous Strong Bond–strong Anharmonicity And Coherent Phonon Transport In The Ultralow Lattice Thermal Conductivity Compounds $X\mathrm{Ag}Y (X=\mathrm{K},\mathrm{Rb},\mathrm{Cs};Y=\mathrm{S},\mathrm{Se},\mathrm{Te})$

tldr: This paper investigates the microscopic origin of ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in layered XAgY compounds through bond-rigidity heterogeneity and anharmonic phonon transport.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic origin of intrinsically low lattice thermal conductivity is crucial for designing thermoelectric materials.
method: The authors perform lattice dynamics and thermal transport calculations, analyzing bond-rigidity heterogeneity and its effect on phonon anharmonicity and coherent transport.
result: They find that bond-rigidity heterogeneity induces anomalous strong bond–strong anharmonicity, leading to ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the design of thermoelectric materials with ultralow thermal conductivity.

tldr: This paper studies anomalous Hall conductivity and magnetostriction in heavy-element substituted Co-based Heusler alloys, focusing on topological transport and magnetoelastic properties.
motivation: To find Heusler alloys with large anomalous Hall conductivity and magnetostriction for spintronic and magnetoelastic applications.
method: Systematic investigation of topological transport properties and magnetostriction in heavy-element substituted Co-based all-d Heusler alloys.
result: Identified alloys with enhanced anomalous Hall conductivity and magnetostriction.
conclusion: These materials are promising for advanced spintronic and magnetoelastic devices.

motivation: To overcome the low Curie temperature of CrI3 for spintronic applications.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory.
result: Intercalation enhances ferromagnetic coupling, raising Curie temperature to near room temperature.
conclusion: Intercalation is a viable strategy to achieve room-temperature ferromagnetism in van der Waals magnets.

title: Pressure-driven Superconductivity And Unexpected Semiconducting Behavior In Li-Pt Electrides
authors: Xinrui Jia, Yao Sun, Ailing Liu, Shoutao Zhang, Xin Zhong, And Hanyu Liu

method: First-principles structure-prediction simulations (e.g., evolutionary algorithms) combined with density functional theory calculations.
result: Identified new Li-Pt compounds that exhibit superconductivity under pressure and unexpected semiconducting behavior in certain phases.
conclusion: Li-Pt electrides show rich pressure-induced electronic transitions, offering insights into electride superconductivity and semiconductor behavior.

title: Probing Magnetic Field Sensitive Criticality In MnP Single Crystals: From Low-field Scaling To High-field Crossover

motivation: To understand the magnetic phase transitions and critical exponents in MnP, a material with potential for magnetocaloric applications.
method: Single crystals were synthesized and characterized using X-ray diffraction, magnetization measurements, and magnetocaloric effect analysis, with scaling analysis of critical exponents.
result: The study reveals low-field scaling behavior and a high-field crossover, providing critical exponents consistent with a 3D Heisenberg model.
conclusion: MnP exhibits field-sensitive criticality that can be tuned for magnetocaloric applications, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without quantum information or thermodynamics connections.

method: First-principles calculations using density functional theory and phonon calculations, analyzing anharmonic effects and phase transitions.
result: Lattice anharmonicity and structural phase transitions significantly modify the Fröhlich interaction strength and screening.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of electron-phonon coupling in perovskites requires inclusion of anharmonicity and phase transition effects.

authors: Ryosuke Kurihara, Atsuhiko Miyata, Koji Araki, Shusaku Imajo, Ruo Hibino, Atsushi Miyake, Sergei Zherlitsyn, Joachim Wosnitza, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Fumitoshi Iga, Masashi Tokunaga, And Yasuhiro H. Matsuda

Quantum oscillations in the Kondo insulator YbB
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235129] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasonic measurements in YbB12 find no magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations in the insulating phase, contrasting with transport and magnetocaloric signals.
motivation: Quantum oscillations in Kondo insulators challenge conventional band theory; the authors aim to resolve inconsistencies by probing elastic constants.
method: High-field ultrasonic measurements of elastic constants in YbB12 single crystals, compared with transport and magnetocaloric data.
result: No magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations were detected in the elastic constant, despite clear oscillations in transport and magnetocaloric measurements.
conclusion: The absence of elastic constant oscillations suggests a non-trivial origin for quantum oscillations in insulators, possibly involving neutral fermions or other exotic states.

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235310] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies paramagnetic instability in a tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit interactions, a condensed matter physics topic without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of electron gases in nanowires with strong spin-orbit coupling.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of an electron gas confined in a thin tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit interaction, deriving critical coupling constants.
result: A critical value of the Rashba coupling constant is found, dependent only on the nanowire radius, at which paramagnetic order becomes unstable.
conclusion: The work describes a specific instability mechanism in nanowires, relevant to spintronics but not to the user's research directions.

title: Spatial Correlations In Susceptible-infected-susceptible Processes On Random Regular Graphs
authors: Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, And Michael Assaf

This constraint naturally gives rise to spatial correlations between the states of neighboring nodes, as the infection status of connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs using pair approximation and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding how network structure and spatial correlations affect epidemic spread is important for predicting disease dynamics.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for spatial correlations using pair approximation and validate them with Monte Carlo simulations on random regular graphs.
result: They find that spatial correlations significantly impact the epidemic threshold and prevalence, and their analytical predictions match simulations well.
conclusion: Spatial correlations are crucial for accurate modeling of SIS processes on networks, and pair approximation provides a useful analytical tool.

title: Propagation Of Coherent Mechanical Waves In Stealth Hyperuniform Materials In The Transparent Regime

method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of wave propagation in stealth hyperuniform elastic media.
result: Identifies conditions for transparency and coherent wave propagation in these materials.
conclusion: Stealth hyperuniform materials can support coherent wave propagation with reduced scattering.

method: The authors use Laplace transform techniques and pole analysis to derive the asymptotic behavior of the radial distribution function at high packing fractions.
result: They show that spatial correlations decay algebraically in strictly 1D systems and exponentially in quasi-1D confined geometries.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for correlation decay in hard-core fluids, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

motivation: Real-world nonautonomous systems like planetary weather have time-varying forcing and discrete observations, requiring adaptive chaos control methods.
method: A stochastic approach is used to identify regimes and control extremes in the nonautonomous Lorenz model, incorporating seasonally and diurnally varying forcing.
result: The method successfully identifies regimes and demonstrates control of extreme events in the model.
conclusion: The approach may be applicable to real-world climate systems for predicting and mitigating extreme weather events.

motivation: To understand the entangled dynamics between species and their environment in ecosystems, where both evolve in space and time.
method: The authors introduce a model coupling persistent random walkers (agents) with a dynamic environment representing a nutrient source, and analyze the resulting spatiotemporal patterns.
result: The model reveals complex feedback loops between agent movement and resource depletion, leading to emergent population behaviors.
conclusion: The study provides insights into ecosystem dynamics but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium assembly of Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes during surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly.
motivation: To understand how polymerization-driven self-assembly on anisotropic templates can produce structured materials under nonequilibrium conditions.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations to model the surface-initiated polymerization on Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes and analyze the resulting assembly dynamics.
result: They identify distinct assembly mechanisms and morphologies depending on grafting density and polymerization rate.
conclusion: The work provides insights into designing nonequilibrium assembly processes for functional nanomaterials.

motivation: Standard jamming models ignore diversity in cell repulsion ranges; this work aims to understand how homotypic repulsion drives percolation and jamming in multitype assemblies.
method: Develops a chromatic percolation model and maps it to mechanical jamming using simulations or theoretical analysis.
result: Establishes a relationship between percolation of like-type particles and mechanical jamming in systems with extended-range homotypic repulsion.
conclusion: Chromatic percolation provides a framework to connect percolation and jamming in diverse particle systems, relevant to biological tissues.
